1.1: In the beginning was that Word, and that Word was with God, and that Word was God.
1.2: This same was in the beginning with God.
1.3: All things were made by it, and without it was made nothing that was made.
1.4: In it was life, and that life was the light of men.
1.5: And that light shineth in the darkenesse, and the darkenesse comprehended it not.
1.6: There was a man sent from God, whose name was John.
1.7: This same came for a witness, to bear witness of that light, that all men through him might beleeue.
1.8: He was not that light, but was sent to bear witness of that light.
1.9: This was that true light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world.
1.10: He was in the world, and the world was made by him: and the world knew him not.
1.11: He came unto his own, and his own received him not.
1.12: But as many as received him, to them he gave prerogatiue to be the sonnes of God, even to them that beleeue in his Name.
1.13: Which are borne not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of ye wil of man, but of God.
1.14: And that Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we saw the glorie thereof, as the glorie of the onely begotten Sonne of the Father) full of grace and trueth.
1.15: John bare witness of him, and cryed, saying, This was he of whom I said, He that cometh after me, was before me: for he was better then I.
1.16: And of his fulness have all we received, and grace for grace.
1.17: For the Law was given by Moses, but grace, and trueth came by Jesus Christ.
1.18: No man hath seen God at any time: that onely begotten Sonne, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.
1.19: Then this is the record of John, when the Iewes sent Priestes and Levites from Hierusalem, to ask him, Who art thou?
1.20: And he confessed and denied not, and said plainely, I am not that Christ.
1.21: And they asked him, What then? Art thou Elias? And he said, I am not. Art thou that Prophet? And he answered, No.
1.22: Then said they unto him, Who art thou, that we may give an answer to them that sent us? What sayest thou of thy self?
1.23: He said, I am the voyce of him that cryeth in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said the Prophet Esaias.
1.24: Now they which were sent, were of the Pharises.
1.25: And they asked him, and said unto him, Why baptizest thou then, if thou be not that Christ, neither Elias, nor that Prophet?
1.26: John answered them, saying, I baptize with water: but there is one among you, whom ye know not.
1.27: He it is that cometh after me, which was before me, whose shoe latchet I am not worthie to unloose.
1.28: These things were done in Bethabara beyond Jordan, where John did baptize.
1.29: The next day John, seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold that Lamb of God, which taketh away the sinne of the world.
1.30: This is he of whom I said, After me cometh a man, which was before me: for he was better then I.
1.31: And I knew him not: but because he should be declared to Israel, therefore am I come, baptizing with water.
1.32: So John bare record, saying, I beheld that Spirit come down from heaven, like a dove, and it abode upon him,
1.33: And I knew him not: but he that sent me to baptize with water, he said unto me, Upon whom thou shalt see that Spirit come down, and tary still on him, that is he which baptizeth with the holy Ghost.
1.34: And I saw, and bare record that this is that Sonne of God.
1.35: The next day, John stood again, and two of his disciples.
1.36: And he beheld Jesus walking by, and said, Behold that Lamb of God.
1.37: And the two disciples heard him speak, and followed Jesus.
1.38: Then Jesus turned about, and saw them follow, and said unto them, What seek ye? And they said unto him, Rabbi (which is to say by interpretation, Master) where dwellest thou?
1.39: He said unto them, Come, and see. They came and saw where hee dwelt, and abode with him that day: for it was about the tenth hour.
1.40: Andrew, Simon Peters brother, was one of the two which had heard it of John, and that followed him.
1.41: The same found his brother Simon first, and said unto him, We have found that Messias, which is by interpretation, that Christ.
1.42: And he brought him to Jesus. And Jesus beheld him, and said, Thou art Simon the sonne of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, a stone.
1.43: The day following, Jesus would goe into Galile, and found Philip, and said unto him, Follow me.
1.44: Now Philip was of Bethsaida, the citie of Andrew and Peter.
1.45: Philippe found Nathanael, and said unto him, Wee have found him of whom Moses did write in the Law, and the Prophetes, Jesus that sonne of Joseph, that was of Nazareth.
1.46: Then Nathanael sayde unto him, Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip said to him, Come, and see.
1.47: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and said of him, Behold in deed an Israelite, in whom is no guile.
1.48: Nathanael sayde unto him, Whence knewest thou mee? Jesus answered, and sayd unto him, Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the figge tree, I saw thee.
1.49: Nathanael answered, and said unto him, Rabbi, thou art that Sonne of God: thou art that King of Israel.
1.50: Jesus answered, and sayde unto him, Because I sayde unto thee, I saw thee under the figtree, beleeuest thou? thou shalt see greater things then these.
1.51: And he said unto him, Verely, verely I say unto you, hereafter shall yee see heaven open, and the Angels of God ascending, and descending upon that Sonne of man.

2.1: And the third day, was there a mariage in Cana a town of Galile, and the mother of Jesus was there.
2.2: And Jesus was called also, and his disciples unto the mariage.
2.3: Now when the wine failed, the mother of Jesus said unto him, They have no wine.
2.4: Jesus said unto her, Woman, what have I to doe with thee? mine hour is not yet come.
2.5: His mother said unto the servants, Whatsoever he sayeth unto you, doe it.
2.6: And there were set there, six waterpots of stone, after the maner of the purifying of the Iewes, conteining two or three firkins a piece.
2.7: And Jesus sayde unto them, Fill the waterpots with water. Then they filled them up to the brim.
2.8: Then he sayde unto them, Draw out now and bear unto the gouernour of the feast. So they bare it.
2.9: Now when the gouernour of the feast had tasted the water that was made wine, (for he knew not whence it was: but the servants, which drew the water, knew) the gouernour of ye feast called the bridegrome,
2.10: And said unto him, All men at the beginning set foorth good wine, and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse: but thou hast kept back the good wine until now.
2.11: This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana a town of Galile, and shewed forth his glorie: and his disciples beleeued on him.
2.12: After that, he went down into Capernaum, he and his mother, and his brethren, and his disciples: but they continued not many daies there.
2.13: For the Iewes Passeouer was at hand. Therefore Jesus went up to Hierusalem.
2.14: And he found in the Temple those that sold oxen, and sheep, and doves, and changers of money, sitting there.
2.15: Then hee made a scourge of small cordes, and drave them all out of the Temple with the sheep and oxen, and powred out the changers money, and overthrew the tables,
2.16: And said unto them that sold doves, Take these things hence: make not my fathers house, an house of marchandise.
2.17: And his disciples remembred, that it was written, The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up.
2.18: Then answered the Iewes, and said unto him, What sign shewest thou unto us, that thou doest these things?
2.19: Jesus answered, and said unto them, Destroy this Temple, and in three daies I will raise it up again.
2.20: Then said the Iewes, Fourtie and six yeeres was this Temple a building, and wilt thou rear it up in three daies?
2.21: But he spake of the temple of his bodie.
2.22: Assoone therefore as he was risen from the dead, his disciples remembred that hee thus sayde unto them: and they beleeued the Scripture, and the word which Jesus had said.
2.23: Now when hee was at Hierusalem at the Passeouer in the feast, many beleeued in his Name, when they saw his miracles which he did.
2.24: But Jesus did not commit him self unto them, because he knew them all,
2.25: And had no need that any should testifie of man: for he knew what was in man.

3.1: There was now a man of the Pharises, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Iewes.
3.2: This man came to Jesus by night, and sayd unto him, Rabbi, we know ye thou art a teacher come from God: for no man could do these miracles that thou doest, except God were with him.
3.3: Jesus answered, and said unto him, Verely, verely I say unto thee, except a man be borne again, he can not see the kingdom of God.
3.4: Nicodemus sayde unto him, How can a man be borne which is old? can he enter into his mothers womb again, and be borne?
3.5: Jesus answered, Verely, verely I say unto thee, except that a man be borne of water and of the Spirit, hee can not enter into the kingdom of God.
3.6: That which is borne of the flesh, is flesh: and that that is borne of the Spirit, is spirit.
3.7: Marueile not that I said to thee, Yee must be borne again.
3.8: The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every man that is borne of the Spirit.
3.9: Nicodemus answered, and said unto him, How can these things be?
3.10: Jesus answered, and said unto him, Art thou a teacher of Israel, and knowest not these things?
3.11: Verely, verely I say unto thee, wee speak that we know, and testifie that we have seen: but yee receive not our witness.
3.12: If when I tel you earthly things, ye beleeue not, how should yee beleeue, if I shall tel you of heavenly things?
3.13: For no man ascendeth up to heaven, but he that hath descended from heaven, that Sonne of man which is in heaven.
3.14: And as Moses lift up the serpent in the wilderness, so must that Sonne of man be lift up,
3.15: That whosoever beleeueth in him, should not perish, but have eternal life.
3.16: For God so loved the world, that hee hath given his onely begotten Sonne, that whosoever beleeueth in him, should not perish, but have everlasting life.
3.17: For God sent not his Sonne into the world, that he should condemn the world, but that the world through him might be saved.
3.18: Hee that beleeueth in him, is not condemned: but hee that beleeueth not, is condemned already, because he hath not beleeued in the Name of that onely begotten Sonne of God.
3.19: And this is the condemnation, that that light came into the world, and men loved darkness rather then that light, because their deedes were evil.
3.20: For every man that evil doeth, hateth the light, neither cometh to light, least his deedes should be reprooued.
3.21: But he that doeth trueth, cometh to the light, that his deedes might bee made manifest, that they are wrought according to God.
3.22: After these things, came Jesus and his disciples into the land of Judea, and there taried with them, and baptized.
3.23: And John also baptized in Enon besides Salim, because there was much water there: and they came, and were baptized.
3.24: For John was not yet cast into prison.
3.25: Then there arose a question between Iohns disciples and the Iewes, about purifying.
3.26: And they came unto John, and said unto him, Rabbi, he that was with thee beyond Iorden, to whom thou barest witness, behold, he baptizeth, and all men come to him.
3.27: John answered, and said, A man can receive nothing, except it be given him from heaven.
3.28: Yee your selves are my witnesses, that I sayde, I am not that Christ, but that I am sent before him.
3.29: He that hath the bride, is the bridegrome: but the friend of the bridegrome which standeth and heareth him, reioyceth greatly, because of the bridegromes voyce. This my joy therefore is fulfilled.
3.30: He must increase, but I must decrease.
3.31: Hee that is come from an hie, is above all: he that is of the earth, is of the earth, and speaketh of the earth: hee that is come from heaven, is above all.
3.32: And what hee hath seen and heard, that he testifieth: but no man receiveth his testimonie.
3.33: He that hath received his testimonie, hath sealed that God is true.
3.34: For hee whom God hath sent, speaketh the woordes of God: for God giveth him not the Spirit by measure.
3.35: The Father loveth the Sonne, and hath given all things into his hand.
3.36: Hee that beleeueth in the Sonne, hath everlasting life, and hee that obeyeth not the Sonne, shall not see life, but the wrath of God abideth on him.

4.1: Now when the Lord knew, how the Pharises had heard, that Jesus made and baptized moe disciples then John,
4.2: (Though Jesus himself baptized not: but his disciples)
4.3: Hee left Judea, and departed again into Galile.
4.4: And he must needes goe through Samaria.
4.5: Then came hee to a citie of Samaria called Sychar, neere unto the possession that Jacob gave to his sonne Joseph.
4.6: And there was Iacobs well. Jesus then wearied in the journey, sat thus on the well: it was about the sixt hour.
4.7: There came a woman of Samaria to draw water. Jesus sayd unto her, Give me drink.
4.8: For his disciples were gone away into the citie, to buy meat.
4.9: Then sayde the woman of Samaria unto him, How is it, that thou being a Iewe, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? For the Iewes meddle not with the Samaritans.
4.10: Jesus answered and said unto her, If thou knewest that gift of God, and who it is that saieth to thee, Give mee drink, thou wouldest have asked of him, and hee would have given thee, water of life.
4.11: The woman said unto him, Sir, thou hast nothing to draw with, and the well is deep: from whence then hast thou that water of life?
4.12: Art thou greater then our father Jacob, which gave us the well, and hee himself drank thereof, and his sonnes, and his cattell?
4.13: Jesus answered, and said unto her, Whosoever drinketh of this water, shall thirst again:
4.14: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him, shall never be more a thirst: but the water that I shall give him, shalbe in him a well of water, springing up into everlasting life.
4.15: The woman said unto him, Syr, give me of that water, that I may not thirst, neither come hither to draw.
4.16: Jesus said unto her, Go, call thine husband, and come hither.
4.17: The woman answered, and said, I have no husband. Jesus said unto her, Thou hast well said, I have no husband.
4.18: For thou hast had five husbands, and he whom thou now hast, is not thine husband: that saidest thou truely.
4.19: The woman said unto him, Sir, I see that thou art a Prophet.
4.20: Our fathers worshipped in this mountain, and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.
4.21: Jesus said unto her, Woman, beleeue me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor at Hierusalem worship ye Father.
4.22: Ye worship that which ye know not: we worship that which we know: for salvation is of the Iewes.
4.23: But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit, and trueth: for the Father requireth even such to worship him.
4.24: God is a Spirit, and they that worship him, must worship him in spirit and trueth.
4.25: The woman said unto him, I know well that Messias shall come which is called Christ: when he is come, he will tell us all things.
4.26: Jesus said unto her, I am he, that speak unto thee.
4.27: And upon that, came his disciples, and marueiled that he talked with a woman: yet no man said unto him, What askest thou? or why talkest thou with her?
4.28: The woman then left her waterpot, and went her way into the citie, and said to the men,
4.29: Come, see a man which hath told me all things that ever I did: is not he that Christ?
4.30: Then they went out of the citie, and came unto him.
4.31: In the mean while, the disciples prayed him, saying, Master, eat.
4.32: But he said unto them, I have meat to eat that ye know not of.
4.33: Then said ye disciples between themselves, Hath any man brought him meat?
4.34: Jesus said unto them, My meat is that I may doe the will of him that sent me, and finish his work.
4.35: Say not ye, There are yet four moneths, and then cometh harvest? Behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the regions: for they are white alreadie unto harvest.
4.36: And he that reapeth, receiveth reward, and gathereth fruit unto life eternal, that both he that soweth, and he that reapeth, might reioyce together.
4.37: For herein is the saying true, that one soweth, and an other reapeth.
4.38: I sent you to reap that, whereon ye bestowed no labour: other men laboured, and ye are entred into their labours.
4.39: Now many of the Samaritans of that citie beleeued in him, for the saying of the woman which testified, He hath told me all things that ever I did.
4.40: Then when the Samaritans were come unto him, they besought him, that he would tarie with them: and he abode there two dayes.
4.41: And many moe beleeued because of his own word.
4.42: And they said unto the woman, Now we beleeue, not because of thy saying: for we have heard him our selves, and know that this is in deed that Christ the Sauiour of the world.
4.43: So two dayes after he departed thence, and went into Galile.
4.44: For Jesus himself had testified, that a Prophet hath none honour in his own countrey.
4.45: Then when he was come into Galile, the Galileans received him, which had seen all the things that he did at Hierusalem at the feast: for they went also unto the feast.
4.46: And Jesus came again into Cana a town of Galile, where he had made of water, wine. And there was a certain ruler, whose sonne was sick at Capernaum.
4.47: When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judea into Galile, he went unto him, and besought him that he would goe down, and heal his sonne: for he was even ready to die.
4.48: Then said Jesus unto him, Except ye see signes and wonders, ye will not beleeue.
4.49: The ruler said unto him, Syr, goe down before my sonne dye.
4.50: Jesus said unto him, Go thy way, thy sonne liveth: and the man beleeued the word that Jesus had spoken unto him, and went his way.
4.51: And as he was now going down, his servants met him, saying, Thy sonne liveth.
4.52: Then enquired he of them the hour when he began to amend. And they said unto him, Yesterday the seventh hour the fever left him.
4.53: Then the father knew, that it was the same hour in the which Jesus had said unto him, Thy sonne liveth. And he beleeued, and all his houshold.
4.54: This second miracle did Jesus again, after he was come out of Judea into Galile.

5.1: After that, there was a feast of the Iewes, and Jesus went up to Hierusalem.
5.2: And there is at Hierusalem by the place of the sheep, a pool called in Ebrew Bethesda, having five porches:
5.3: In the which lay a great multitude of sick folk, of blind, halt, and withered, wayting for the moving of the water.
5.4: For an Angel went down at a certain season into the pool, and troubled the water: whosoever then first, after the stirring of the water, stepped in, was made whole of whatsoever disease he had.
5.5: And a certain man was there, which had been diseased eight and thirtie yeeres.
5.6: When Jesus saw him lie, and knew that he now long time had been diseased, he said unto him, Wilt thou be made whole?
5.7: The sick man answered him, Sir, I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the pool: but while I am coming, another steppeth down before me.
5.8: Jesus said unto him, Rise: take up thy bed, and walk.
5.9: And immediatly the man was made whole, and took up his bed, and walked: and the same day was the Sabbath.
5.10: The Iewes therefore said to him that was made whole, It is the Sabbath day: it is not lawful for thee to cary thy bed.
5.11: He answered them, He that made me whole, he said unto me, Take up thy bed, and walk.
5.12: Then asked they him, What man is that which said unto thee, Take up thy bed and walk?
5.13: And he that was healed, knew not who it was: for Jesus had conueied himself away from the multitude that was in that place.
5.14: And after that, Jesus found him in the Temple, and said unto him, Behold, thou art made whole: sinne no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.
5.15: The man departed and told the Iewes that it was Jesus, which had made him whole.
5.16: And therefore the Iewes did persecute Jesus, and sought to slay him, because he had done these things on the Sabbath day.
5.17: But Jesus answered them, My Father worketh hitherto, and I work.
5.18: Therefore the Iewes sought the more to kill him: not onely because he had broken the Sabbath: but said also that God was his Father, and made himself equal with God.
5.19: Then answered Jesus, and said unto them, Verely, verely I say unto you, The Sonne can doe nothing of himself, save that he seeth the Father doe: for whatsoever things he doth, the same things doeth the Sonne in like maner.
5.20: For the Father loveth the Sonne, and sheweth him all things, whatsoever he himself doeth, and he will shew him greater workes then these, that ye should marueile.
5.21: For likewise as the Father rayseth up the dead, and quickeneth them, so the Sonne quickeneth whom he will.
5.22: For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all iudgement unto the Sonne,
5.23: Because that all men should honour the Sonne, as they honour the Father: he that honoureth not the Sonne, the same honoureth not the Father, which hath sent him.
5.24: Verely, verely I say unto you, he that heareth my word, and beleeueth him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation, but hath passed from death unto life.
5.25: Verely, verely I say unto you, the hour shall come, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voyce of the Sonne of God: and they that hear it, shall live.
5.26: For as the Father hath life in himself, so likewise hath he given to the Sonne to have life in himself,
5.27: And hath given him power also to execute iudgement, in that he is the Sonne of man.
5.28: Marueile not at this: for the hour shall come, in the which all that are in the graves, shall hear his voyce.
5.29: And they shall come foorth, that have done good, unto ye resurrection of life: but they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of condemnation.
5.30: I can doe nothing of mine own self: as I hear, I judge: and my iudgement is just, because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father who hath sent me.
5.31: If I should bear witness of my self, my witness were not true.
5.32: There is another that beareth witness of me, and I know that the witness, which he beareth of me, is true.
5.33: Ye sent unto John, and he bare witness unto the trueth.
5.34: But I receive not the record of man: nevertheless these things I say, that ye might be saved.
5.35: He was a burning, and a shining candle: and ye would for a season have reioyced in his light.
5.36: But I have greater witness then the witness of John: for the workes which the Father hath given me to finish, the same workes that I doe, bear witness of me, that the Father sent me.
5.37: And the Father himself, which hath sent me, beareth witness of me. Ye have not heard his voyce at any time, neither have ye seen his shape.
5.38: And his word have you not abiding in you: for whom he hath sent, him ye beleeued not.
5.39: Search the Scriptures: for in them ye think to have eternal life, and they are they which testifie of me.
5.40: But ye will not come to me, that ye might have life.
5.41: I receive not the prayse of men.
5.42: But I know you, that ye have not the love of God in you.
5.43: I am come in my Fathers Name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him will ye receive.
5.44: How can ye beleeue, which receive honour one of another, and seek not the honour that cometh of God alone?
5.45: Doe not think that I will accuse you to my Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust.
5.46: For had ye beleeued Moses, ye would have beleeued me: for he wrote of me.
5.47: But if ye beleeue not his writings, how shall ye beleeue my wordes?

6.1: After these thinges, Jesus went his way over the sea of Galile, which is Tiberias.
6.2: And a great multitude followed him, because they saw his miracles, which hee did on them that were diseased.
6.3: Then Jesus went up into a mountain, and there he sat with his disciples.
6.4: Now the Passeouer, a feast of the Iewes, was neere.
6.5: Then Jesus lift up his eyes, and seeing that a great multitude came unto him, hee sayde unto Philippe, Whence shall we buy bread, that these might eat?
6.6: (And this he sayde to prooue him: for hee himself knew what he would doe.)
6.7: Philippe answered him, Two hundreth penie worth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one of them may take a litle.
6.8: Then said unto him one of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peters brother,
6.9: There is a little boy heere, which hath five barlie loaves, and two fishes: but what are they among so many?
6.10: And Jesus said, Make ye people sit down. (Now there was much grass in that place.) Then the men sat down in nomber, about five thousand.
6.11: And Jesus took the bread, and gave thanks, and gave to the disciples, and the disciples, to them that were set down: and likewise of the fishes as much as they would.
6.12: And when they were satisfied, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the broken meat which remaineth, that nothing be lost.
6.13: Then they gathered it together, and filled twelve baskets with the broken meat of the five barly loaves, which remained unto them that had eaten.
6.14: Then the men, when they had seen the miracle that Jesus did, said, This is of a trueth that Prophet that should come into the world.
6.15: When Jesus therfore perceived that they would come, and take him to make him a King, hee departed again into a mountain himself alone.
6.16: When even was now come, his disciples went down unto the sea,
6.17: And entred into a shippe, and went over the sea, towardes Capernaum: and now it was dark, and Jesus was not come to them.
6.18: And the Sea arose with a great wind that blew.
6.19: And when they had rowed about five and twentie, or thirtie furlongs, they saw Jesus walking on the sea, and drawing neere unto the ship: so they were afraid.
6.20: But he said unto them, It is I: be not afraid.
6.21: Then willingly they received him into the ship, and the ship was by and by at the land, whither they went.
6.22: The day following, the people which stood on the other side of the sea, saw that there was none other ship there, save that one, whereinto his disciples were entred, and that Jesus went not with his disciples in the ship, but that his disciples were gone alone,
6.23: And that there came other ships from Tiberias neere unto the place where they ate the bread, after the Lord had given thankes.
6.24: Now when the people saw that Jesus was not there, neither his disciples, they also took shipping, and came to Capernaum, seeking for Jesus.
6.25: And when they had found him on the other side of the sea, they sayde unto him, Rabbi, when camest thou hither?
6.26: Jesus answered them; and sayde, Verely, verely I say unto you, ye seek me not because ye saw the miracles, but because yee ate of ye loaves, and were filled.
6.27: Labour not for ye meat which perisheth, but for the meat that endureth unto everlasting life, which the Sonne of man shall give unto you: for him hath God the Father sealed.
6.28: Then sayde they unto him, What shall we doe, that we might work the workes of God?
6.29: Jesus answered, and sayde unto them, This is the woorke of God, that yee beleeue in him, whom he hath sent.
6.30: They sayde therefore unto him, What sign shewest thou then, that we may see it, and beleeue thee? what doest thou woorke?
6.31: Our fathers did eat Manna in the desart, as it is written, Hee gave them bread from heaven to eat.
6.32: Then Jesus said unto them, Verely, verely I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven, but my Father giveth you that true bread from heaven.
6.33: For the bread of God is hee which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.
6.34: Then they said unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread.
6.35: And Jesus said unto them, I am that bread of life: he that cometh to me, shall not hunger, and he that beleeueth in me, shall never thirst.
6.36: But I said unto you, that ye also have seen me, and beleeue not.
6.37: All that the Father giveth me, shall come to mee: and him that cometh to me, I cast not away.
6.38: For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own wil, but his wil which hath sent me.
6.39: And this is the Fathers will which hath sent mee, that of all which hee hath given mee, I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day.
6.40: And this is the will of him that sent mee, that every man which seeth the Sonne, and beleeueth in him, should have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.
6.41: The Iewes then murmured at him because hee sayde, I am that bread, which is come down from heaven.
6.42: And they said, Is not this Jesus that sonne of Joseph, whose father and mother wee know? how then sayth he, I came down from heaven?
6.43: Jesus then answered, and said unto them, Murmur not among your selves.
6.44: No man can come to mee, except the Father, which hath sent mee, draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day.
6.45: It is written in the Prophetes, And they shalbe al taught of God. Every man therefore that hath heard, and hath learned of the Father, cometh unto me:
6.46: Not that any man hath seen the Father, save hee which is of God, hee hath seen the Father.
6.47: Verely, verely I say unto you, hee that beleeueth in me, hath everlasting life.
6.48: I am that bread of life.
6.49: Your fathers did eat Manna in the wilderness, and are dead.
6.50: This is that bread, which cometh down from heaven, that hee which eateth of it, should not die.
6.51: I am that living bread, which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, hee shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give, is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world.
6.52: Then the Iewes strove among themselves, saying, How can this man give us his flesh to eat?
6.53: Then Jesus said unto them, Verely, verely I say unto you, Except yee eat the flesh of the Sonne of man, and drink his blood, yee have no life in you.
6.54: Whosoever eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, hath eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.
6.55: For my flesh is meat in deed, and my blood is drink in deed.
6.56: Hee that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, dwelleth in me, and I in him.
6.57: As that living Father hath sent me, so live I by the Father, and he that eateth me, even he shall live by me.
6.58: This is that bread which came down from heaven: not as your fathers have eaten Manna, and are dead. Hee that eateth of this bread, shall live for ever.
6.59: These things spake he in the Synagogue, as he taught in Capernaum.
6.60: Many therefore of his disciples (when they heard this) sayde, This is an hard saying: who can hear it?
6.61: But Jesus knowing in himself, that his disciples murmured at this, said unto them, Doeth this offend you?
6.62: What then if yee should see that Sonne of man ascend up where he was before?
6.63: It is the spirit that quickeneth: the flesh profiteth nothing: the woordes that I speak unto you, are spirit and life.
6.64: But there are some of you that beleeue not: for Jesus knew from the beginning, which they were that beleeued not, and who should betray him.
6.65: And hee said, Therefore said I unto you, that no man can come unto mee, except it be given unto him of my Father.
6.66: From that time, many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him.
6.67: Then sayde Jesus to the twelve, Will yee also goe away?
6.68: Then Simon Peter answered him, Master, to whom shall we goe? thou hast the wordes of eternal life:
6.69: And we beleeue and know that thou art that Christ that Sonne of the living God.
6.70: Jesus answered them, Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil?
6.71: Now he spake it of Judas Iscariot the sonne of Simon: for hee it was that should betraie him, though he was one of the twelve.

7.1: After these things, Jesus walked in Galile, and would not walk in Judea: for the Iewes sought to kill him.
7.2: Now the Iewes feast of the Tabernacles was at hand.
7.3: His brethren therefore sayde unto him, Depart hence, and goe into Judea, that thy disciples may see thy woorkes that thou doest.
7.4: For there is no man that doeth any thing secretely, and hee himself seeketh to be famous. If thou doest these things, shew thy self to the world.
7.5: For as yet his brethren beleeued not in him.
7.6: Then Jesus said unto them, My time is not yet come: but your time is alway readie.
7.7: The world can not hate you: but me it hateth, because I testifie of it, that the workes thereof are evil.
7.8: Go ye up unto this feast: I wil not go up yet unto this feast: for my time is not yet fulfilled.
7.9: These things he sayde unto them, and abode still in Galile.
7.10: But assoone as his brethren were gone up, then went hee also up unto the feast, not openly, but as it were priuilie.
7.11: Then the Iewes sought him at the feast, and said, Where is hee?
7.12: And much murmuring was there of him among the people. Some said, He is a good man: other sayd, Nay: but he deceiveth the people.
7.13: Howbeit no man spake openly of him for fear of the Iewes.
7.14: Now when half the feast was done, Jesus went up into the Temple and taught.
7.15: And the Iewes marueiled, saving, How knoweth this man the Scriptures, seeing that hee never learned!
7.16: Jesus answered them, and said, My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me.
7.17: If any man will doe his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of my self.
7.18: Hee that speaketh of himself, seeketh his own glorie: but hee that seeketh his glory that sent him, the same is true, and no vnrighteousnes is in him.
7.19: Did not Moses give you a Law, and yet none of you keepeth the law? Why goe ye about to kill me?
7.20: The people answered, and said, Thou hast a devil: who goeth about to kill thee?
7.21: Jesus answered, and said to them, I have done one work, and ye all maruaile.
7.22: Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision, (not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers) and ye on the Sabbath day circumcise a man.
7.23: If a man on the Sabbath receive circumcision, that the Law of Moses should not be broken, be ye angrie with me, because I have made a man every whit whole on the Sabbath day?
7.24: Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous iudgement.
7.25: Then said some of them of Hierusalem, Is not this he, whom they goe about to kill?
7.26: And behold, he speaketh openly, and they say nothing to him: doe the rulers know in deed that this is in deed that Christ?
7.27: Howbeit we know this man whence he is: but when that Christ cometh, no man shall know whence he is.
7.28: Then cried Jesus in the Temple as hee taught, saying, Ye both know mee, and know whence I am: yet am I not come of my self, but he that sent me, is true, whom ye know not.
7.29: But I know him: for I am of him, and he hath sent me.
7.30: Then they sought to take him, but no man layde handes on him, because his hour was not yet come.
7.31: Now many of the people beleeued in him, and said, When that Christ cometh, will he doe moe miracles then this man hath done?
7.32: The Pharises heard that the people murmured these thinges of him, and the Pharises, and high Priestes sent officers to take him.
7.33: Then said Jesus unto them, Yet am I a little while with you, and then goe I unto him that sent mee.
7.34: Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me, and where I am, can ye not come.
7.35: Then said the Iewes amongs themselves, Whither will he goe, that we shall not find him? Will he goe unto them that are dispersed among the Grecians, and teach the Grecians?
7.36: What saying is this that hee said, Ye shall seek mee, and shall not find mee? and where I am, cannot ye come?
7.37: Now in the last and great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink.
7.38: Hee that beleeueth in mee, as saith the Scripture, out of his bellie shall flow rivers of water of life.
7.39: (This spake hee of the Spirit which they that beleeued in him, should receive: for the holy Ghost was not yet given, because that Jesus was not yet glorified.)
7.40: So many of the people, when they heard this saying, said, Of a trueth this is that Prophet.
7.41: Other said, This is that Christ: and some said, But shall that Christ come out of Galile?
7.42: Saith not the Scripture that that Christ shall come of the seed of David, and out of the town of Beth-leem, where David was?
7.43: So was there dissension among the people for him.
7.44: And some of them would have taken him, but no man layde handes on him.
7.45: Then came the officers to the hie Priests and Pharises, and they said unto them, Why have ye not brought him?
7.46: The officers answered, Never man spake like this man.
7.47: Then answered them the Pharises, Are yee also deceived?
7.48: Doeth any of the rulers, or of the Pharises beleeue in him?
7.49: But this people, which know not the Law, are cursed.
7.50: Nicodemus said unto them, (he that came to Jesus by night, and was one of them.)
7.51: Doth our Law judge a man before it hear him, and know what he hath done?
7.52: They answered, and said unto him, Art thou also of Galile? Search and look: for out of Galile ariseth no Prophet.
7.53: And every man wet unto his own house.

8.1: And Jesus went unto the mount of Olives,
8.2: And early in the morning came again into the Temple, and all the people came unto him, and he sat down, and taught them.
8.3: Then the Scribes, and the Pharises brought unto him a woman, taken in adulterie, and set her in the middes,
8.4: And said unto him, Master, we foud this woman committing adulterie, even in the very act.
8.5: Now Moses in our Law commanded, that such should be stoned: what sayest thou therefore?
8.6: And this they said to tempt him, that they might have, whereof to accuse him. But Jesus stouped down, and with his finger wrote on the groud.
8.7: And while they continued asking him, hee lift himself up, and sayde unto them, Let him that is among you without sinne, cast the first stone at her.
8.8: And again hee stouped down, and wrote on the ground.
8.9: And when they heard it, being accused by their own conscience, they went out one by one, beginning at ye eldest even to the last: so Jesus was left alone, and the woman standing in the mids.
8.10: When Jesus had lift up himself again, and saw no man, but the woman, hee said unto her, Woman, where are those thine accusers? hath no man condemned thee?
8.11: She said, No man, Lord. And Jesus said, Neither do I condemn thee: go and sinne no more.
8.12: Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am that light of the world: hee that followeth mee, shall not walk in darkenes, but shall have that light of life.
8.13: The Pharises therefore said unto him, Thou bearest record of thy self: thy record is not true.
8.14: Jesus answered, and sayde unto them, Though I bear record of my self, yet my record is true: for I know whence I came, and whither I go: but ye cannot tell whence I come, and whither I goe.
8.15: Ye judge after the flesh: I judge no man.
8.16: And if I also judge, my iudgement is true: for I am not alone, but I, and the Father, that sent mee.
8.17: And it is also written in your Law, that the testimonie of two men is true.
8.18: I am one that bear witnes of my self, and the Father that sent me, beareth witnes of me.
8.19: Then said they unto him, Where is that Father of thine? Jesus answered, Ye neither know me, nor that Father of mine. If ye had knowen me, ye should have knowen that Father of mine also.
8.20: These wordes spake Jesus in the treasurie, as hee taught in the Temple, and no man layde handes on him: for his hour was not yet come.
8.21: Then said Jesus again unto them, I goe my way, and ye shall seek me, and shall die in your sinnes, Whither I goe, can ye not come.
8.22: Then said the Iewes, Will he kill himself, because he saith, Whither I goe, can ye not come?
8.23: And hee said unto them, Ye are from beneath, I am from above: ye are of this world, I am not of this world.
8.24: I said therefore unto you, That ye shall die in your sinnes: for except ye beleeue, that I am he, ye shall die in your sinnes.
8.25: Then said they unto him, Who art thou? And Jesus said unto them, Even the same thing that I said unto you from the beginning.
8.26: I have many things to say, and to judge of you: but he that sent me, is true, and the things that I have heard of him, those speak I to the world.
8.27: They vnderstoode not that hee spake to them of the Father.
8.28: Then said Jesus unto them, When ye have lift up the Sonne of man, then shall ye know that I am he, and that I doe nothing of my self, but as my Father hath taught me, so I speak these things.
8.29: For he that sent me, is with me: the Father hath not left me alone, because I do alwayes those things that please him.
8.30: As hee spake these thinges, many beleeued in him.
8.31: Then said Jesus to the Iewes which beleeued in him, If ye continue in my word, ye are verely my disciples,
8.32: And shall know the trueth, and the trueth shall make you free.
8.33: They answered him, Wee be Abrahams seed, and were never bond to any man: why sayest thou then, Ye shalbe made free?
8.34: Jesus answered them, Verely, verely I say unto you, that whosoever committeth sinne, is the servant of sinne.
8.35: And the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the Sonne abideth for ever.
8.36: If that Sonne therefore shall make you free, ye shalbe free in deed.
8.37: I know that ye are Abrahams seed, but yee seek to kill mee, because my word hath no place in you.
8.38: I speak that which I have seen with my Father: and ye doe that which ye have seen with your father.
8.39: They answered, and said unto him, Abraham is our father. Jesus said unto them, If ye were Abrahams children, ye would doe the workes of Abraham.
8.40: But now ye goe about to kill mee, a man that have told you the trueth, which I have heard of God: this did not Abraham.
8.41: Ye do the workes of your father. Then said they to him, We are not borne of fornication: we have one Father, which is God.
8.42: Therefore Jesus sayde unto them, If God were your Father, then would ye love mee: for I proceeded foorth, and came from God, neither came I of my self, but he sent me.
8.43: Why doe ye not vnderstande my talk? because ye cannot hear my word.
8.44: Ye are of your father the devil, and the lustes of your father ye will doe: hee hath been a murtherer from the beginning, and abode not in the trueth, because there is no trueth in him. When hee speaketh a lie, then speaketh hee of his own: for he is a liar, and the father thereof.
8.45: And because I tell you the trueth, yee beleeue me not.
8.46: Which of you can rebuke me of sinne? and if I say the trueth, why do ye not beleeue me?
8.47: He that is of God, heareth Gods wordes: yee therefore hear them not, because ye are not of God.
8.48: Then answered the Iewes, and said unto him, Say we not well that thou art a Samaritan, and hast a devil?
8.49: Jesus answered, I have not a devil, but I honour my Father, and ye have dishonoured me.
8.50: And I seek not mine own praise: but there is one that seeketh it, and judgeth.
8.51: Verely, verely I say unto you, If a man keep my word, he shall never see death.
8.52: Then said the Iewes to him, Now know we that thou hast a devil. Abraham is dead, and the Prophets: and thou sayest, If a man keep my word, he shall never taste of death.
8.53: Art thou greater then our father Abraham, which is dead? and the Prophets are dead: whom makest thou thy self?
8.54: Jesus answered, If I honour my self, mine honour is nothing worth: it is my Father that honoureth me, whom ye say, that hee is your God.
8.55: Yet ye have not knowen him: but I know him, and if I should say I know him not, I should be a liar like unto you: but I know him, and keep his word.
8.56: Your father Abraham reioyced to see my day, and he saw it, and was glad.
8.57: Then sayd ye Iewes unto him, Thou art not yet fiftie yeere old, and hast thou seen Abraham?
8.58: Jesus sayd unto them, Verely, verely I say unto you, before Abraham was, I am.
8.59: Then took they up stones, to cast at him, but Jesus hid himself, and went out of the Temple: And hee passed through the middes of them, and so went his way.

9.1: And as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind from his birth.
9.2: And his disciples asked him, saying, Master, who did sinne, this man, or his parents, that he was borne blind?
9.3: Jesus answered, Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents, but that the workes of God should be shewed on him.
9.4: I must work the workes of him that sent me, while it is day: the night cometh when no man can work.
9.5: As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.
9.6: Assoone as he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spettle, and anointed the eyes of the blind with the clay,
9.7: And sayd unto him, Go wash in the pool of Siloam (which is by interpretation, Sent.) He went his way therefore, and washed, and came again seeing.
9.8: Now the neighbours and they that had seen him before, when he was blind, sayd, Is not this he that sat and begged?
9.9: Some said, This is he: and other sayd, He is like him: but he himself sayd, I am he.
9.10: Therefore they sayd unto him, How were thine eyes opened?
9.11: He answered, and sayd, The man that is called Jesus, made clay, and anointed mine eyes, and sayde unto me, Goe to the pool of Siloam and wash. So I went and washed, and received sight.
9.12: Then they sayd unto him, Where is he? He sayd, I can not tell.
9.13: They brought to the Pharises him that was once blind.
9.14: And it was the Sabbath day, when Jesus made the clay, and opened his eyes.
9.15: Then again the Pharises also asked him, how he had received sight. And hee sayd unto them, He layd clay upon mine eyes, and I washed, and doe see.
9.16: Then said some of the Pharises, This man is not of God, because he keepeth not the Sabbath day. Others sayd, How can a man that is a sinner, doe such miracles? and there was a dissension among them.
9.17: Then spake they unto the blind again, What sayest thou of him, because he hath opened thine eyes? And he sayd, He is a Prophet.
9.18: Then the Iewes did not beleeue him (that he had been blind, and received his sight) until they had called the parents of him that had received sight.
9.19: And they asked them, saying, Is this your sonne, whom ye say was borne blind? How doeth he now see then?
9.20: His parents answered them, and sayd, We know that this is our sonne, and that he was borne blind:
9.21: But by what meanes hee now seeth, we know not: or who hath opened his eyes, can we not tell: he is old ynough: ask him: hee shall answer for himself.
9.22: These wordes spake his parents, because they feared the Iewes: for the Iewes had ordeined already, that if any man did confess that he was Christ, he should be excommunicate out of the Synagogue.
9.23: Therefore sayde his parents, Hee is old ynough: ask him.
9.24: Then again called they the man that had been blind, and sayd unto him, Give glory unto God: we know that this man is a sinner.
9.25: Then he answered, and sayd, Whether hee be a sinner or no, I can not tell: one thing I know, that I was blind, and now I see.
9.26: Then sayd they to him again, What did he to thee? how opened he thine eyes?
9.27: Hee answered them, I have told you already, and yee have not heard it: wherefore would yee hear it again? will yee also be his disciples?
9.28: Then reviled they him, and sayd, Be thou his disciple: we be Moses disciples.
9.29: We know that God spake with Moses: but this man we know not from whence he is.
9.30: The man answered, and sayde unto them, Doutlesse, this is a marueilous thing, that ye know not whence he is, and yet he hath opened mine eyes.
9.31: Now we know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doeth his will, him heareth he.
9.32: Since the world began, was it not heard, that any man opened the eyes of one that was borne blind.
9.33: If this man were not of God, hee could have done nothing.
9.34: They answered, and sayd unto him, Thou art altogether borne in sinnes, and doest thou teach us? so they cast him out.
9.35: Jesus heard that they had cast him out: and when he had found him, he sayd unto him, Doest thou beleeue in the Sonne of God?
9.36: He answered, and sayd, Who is he, Lord, that I might beleeue in him?
9.37: And Jesus sayd unto him, Both thou hast seen him, and he it is that talketh with thee.
9.38: Then he sayd, Lord, I beleeue, and worshipped him.
9.39: And Jesus sayd, I am come unto iudgement into this world, that they which see not, might see: and that they which see, might be made blind.
9.40: And some of the Pharises which were with him, heard these things, and sayd unto him, Are we blind also?
9.41: Jesus sayd unto them, If ye were blind, ye should not have sinne: but now ye say, We see: therefore your sinne remaineth.

10.1: Verely, verely I say unto you, Hee that entreth not in by the door into the sheepefolde, but climeth up another way, he is a theefe and a robber.
10.2: But he that goeth in by the door, is the shepheard of the sheep.
10.3: To him the porter openeth, and the sheep hear his voyce, and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out.
10.4: And when hee hath sent foorth his own sheep, he goeth before them, and the sheep follow him: for they know his voyce.
10.5: And they will not follow a stranger, but they flee from him: for they know not the voyce of strangers.
10.6: This parable spake Jesus unto them: but they vnderstoode not what things they were which he spake unto them.
10.7: Then sayd Jesus unto them again, Verely, verely I say unto you, I am that door of the sheep.
10.8: All, that ever came before me, are theeues and robbers: but the sheep did not hear them.
10.9: I am that door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in, and go out, and find pasture.
10.10: The theefe cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and have it in abundance.
10.11: I am that good shepheard: that good shepheard giveth his life for his sheep.
10.12: But an hireling, and hee which is not the shepheard, neither the sheep are his own, seeth the wolf coming, and hee leaveth the sheep, and fleeth, and the wolf catcheth them, and scattreth the sheep.
10.13: So the hireling fleeth, because he is an hireling, and careth not for the sheep.
10.14: I am that good shepheard, and know mine, and am knowen of mine.
10.15: As the Father knoweth me, so know I the Father: and I lay down my life for my sheep.
10.16: Other sheep I have also, which are not of this fold: them also must I bring, and they shall hear my voyce: and there shalbe one sheepefolde, and one shepheard.
10.17: Therefore doeth my Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I might take it again.
10.18: No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of my self: I have power to lay it down, and have power to take it again: this commandement have I received of my Father.
10.19: Then there was a dissension again among the Iewes for these sayings,
10.20: And many of them sayd, He hath a devil, and is mad: why hear ye him?
10.21: Other sayd, These are not the wordes of him that hath a devil: can the devil open the eyes of the blind?
10.22: And it was at Hierusalem the feast of the Dedication, and it was winter.
10.23: And Jesus walked in the Temple, in Salomons porch.
10.24: Then came the Iewes round about him, and sayd unto him, How long doest thou make us dout? If thou be that Christ, tell us plainely.
10.25: Jesus answered them, I told you, and ye beleeue not: the workes that I doe in my Fathers Name, they bear witnes of me.
10.26: But ye beleeue not: for ye are not of my sheep, as I sayd unto you.
10.27: My sheep hear my voyce, and I know them, and they follow me,
10.28: And I give unto them eternal life, and they shall never perish, neither shall any pluck them out of mine hand.
10.29: My Father which gave them me, is greater then all, and none is able to take them out of my Fathers hand.
10.30: I and my Father are one.
10.31: Then ye Iewes again took up stones, to stone him.
10.32: Jesus answered them, Many good workes have I shewed you from my Father: for which of these workes doe ye stone me?
10.33: The Iewes answered him, saying, For the good work we stone thee not, but for blasphemie, and that thou being a man, makest thy self God.
10.34: Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your Law, I sayd, Ye are gods?
10.35: If hee called them gods, unto whom the word of God was given, and the Scripture cannot be broken,
10.36: Say ye of him, whom the Father hath sanctified, and sent into the world, Thou blasphemest, because I said, I am the Sonne of God?
10.37: If I doe not the workes of my Father, beleeue me not.
10.38: But if I doe, then though ye beleeue not mee, yet beleeue the workes, that ye may know and beleeue, that the Father is in me, and I in him.
10.39: Again they went about to take him: but he escaped out of their handes,
10.40: And went again beyond Jordan, into the place where John first baptized, and there abode.
10.41: And many resorted unto him, and said, John did no miracle: but all thinges that John spake of this man, were true.
10.42: And many beleeued in him there.

11.1: And a certain man was sick, named Lazarus of Bethania, the town of Marie, and her sister Martha.
11.2: (And it was that Mary which anointed the Lord with oyntment, and wiped his feet with her hear, whose brother Lazarus was sick.)
11.3: Therefore his sisters sent unto him, saying, Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest, is sick.
11.4: When Jesus heard it, he said, This sickenes is not unto death, but for the glorie of God, that the Sonne of God might be glorified thereby.
11.5: Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister, and Lazarus.
11.6: And after he had heard that he was sick, yet abode hee two dayes still in the same place where he was.
11.7: Then after that, said he to his disciples, Let us goe into Judea again.
11.8: The disciples said unto him, Master, the Iewes lately sought to stone thee, and doest thou goe thither again?
11.9: Jesus answered, Are there not twelve houres in the day? If a man walk in the day, hee stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world.
11.10: But if a man walk in the night, hee stumbleth, because there is no light in him.
11.11: These things spake he, and after, he said unto them, Our friend Lazarus sleepeth: but I goe to wake him up.
11.12: Then said his disciples, Lord, if he sleep, he shalbe safe.
11.13: Howbeit, Jesus spake of his death: but they thought that he had spoken of the natural sleep.
11.14: Then said Jesus unto them plainely, Lazarus is dead.
11.15: And I am glad for your sakes, that I was not there, that ye may beleeue: but let us go unto him.
11.16: Then said Thomas (which is called Didymus) unto his felow disciples, Let us also goe, that we may die with him.
11.17: Then came Jesus, and found that he had lien in the grave four dayes alreadie.
11.18: (Now Bethania was neere unto Hierusalem, about fifteen furlongs off.)
11.19: And many of ye Iewes were come to Martha and Marie to comfort them for their brother.
11.20: Then Martha, when she heard that Jesus was coming, went to meet him: but Mary sat still in the house.
11.21: Then said Martha unto Jesus, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not been dead.
11.22: But now I know also, that whatsoever thou askest of God, God will give it thee.
11.23: Jesus said unto her, Thy brother shall rise again.
11.24: Martha said unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.
11.25: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection and the life: he that beleeueth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live.
11.26: And whosoever liveth, and beleeueth in me, shall never die: Beleeuest thou this?
11.27: She said unto him, Yea, Lord, I beleeue that thou art that Christ that Sonne of God, which should come into the world.
11.28: And when she had so said, she went her way, and called Mary her sister secretly, saying, The Master is come, and calleth for thee.
11.29: And when she heard it, she arose quickly, and came unto him.
11.30: For Jesus was not yet come into the town, but was in the place where Martha met him.
11.31: The Iewes then which were with her in the house, and comforted her, when they saw Marie, that she rose up hastily, and went out, folowed her, saying, She goeth unto the grave, to weep there.
11.32: Then when Mary was come where Jesus was, and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying unto him, Lord, if thou haddest been here, my brother had not been dead.
11.33: When Jesus therefore saw her weep, and the Iewes also weep which came with her, hee groned in the spirit, and was troubled in himself,
11.34: And said, Where have ye layde him? They said unto him, Lord, come and see.
11.36: Then said the Iewes, Behold, how he loved him.
11.37: And some of them said, Could not he, which opened the eyes of the blind, have made also, that this man should not have died?
11.38: Jesus therefore again groned in himself, and came to the grave. And it was a cave, and a stone was layde upon it.
11.39: Jesus said, Take ye away the stone. Martha the sister of him that was dead, said unto him, Lord, he stinketh alreadie: for he hath been dead four dayes.
11.40: Jesus said unto her, Said I not unto thee, that if thou diddest beleeue, thou shouldest see the glorie of God?
11.41: Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead was layde. And Jesus lift up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee, because thou hast heard me.
11.42: I know that thou hearest me alwayes, but because of the people that stand by, I said it, that they may beleeue, that thou hast sent me.
11.43: As hee had spoken these things, hee cried with a loud voyce, Lazarus, come foorth.
11.44: Then he that was dead, came forth, bound hand and foot with bandes, and his face was bound with a napkin. Jesus said unto them, Loose him, and let him goe.
11.45: Then many of the Iewes, which came to Mary, and had seen the thinges, which Jesus did, beleeued in him.
11.46: But some of them went their way to the Pharises, and told them what things Jesus had done.
11.47: Then gathered the hie Priests, and the Pharises a council, and said, What shall we doe? For this man doeth many miracles.
11.48: If we let him thus alone, all men will beleeue in him, and the Romanes will come and take away both our place, and the nation.
11.49: Then one of them named Caiaphas, which was the hie Priest that same yere, said unto them, Ye perceive nothing at all,
11.50: Nor yet doe you consider that it is expedient for us, that one man die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.
11.51: This spake hee not of himself: but being hie Priest that same yere, he prophecied that Jesus should die for that nation:
11.52: And not for that nation onely, but that he should gather together in one the children of God, which were scattered.
11.53: Then from that day foorth they consulted together, to put him to death.
11.54: Jesus therefore walked no more openly among the Iewes, but went thence unto a countrey neere to the wildernes, into a citie called Ephraim, and there continued with his disciples.
11.55: And the Iewes Passeouer was at hand, and many went out of the countrey up to Hierusalem before the Passeouer, to purifie themselves.
11.56: Then sought they for Jesus, and spake among themselves, as they stood in the Temple, What think ye, that he cometh not to the feast?
11.57: Now both the high Priestes and the Pharises had given a commandement, that if any man knew where he were, he should shew it, that they might take him.

12.1: Then Jesus, six dayes before the Passeouer, came to Bethania, where Lazarus was, who died, whom he had raised from the dead.
12.2: There they made him a supper, and Martha served: but Lazarus was one of them that sat at the table with him.
12.3: Then took Mary a pound of oyntment of Spikenard very costly, and anoynted Jesus feet, and wiped his feet with her hear, and the house was filled with the sauour of the oyntment.
12.4: Then said one of his disciples, even Judas Iscariot Simons sonne, which should betray him:
12.5: Why was not this oyntment sold for three hundreth pence, and given to the poor?
12.6: Now he said this, not that he cared for the poor, but because hee was a theefe, and had the bagge, and bare that which was given.
12.7: Then said Jesus, Let her alone: against the day of my burying she kept it.
12.8: For the poor alwayes yee have with you, but me ye shall not have alwayes.
12.9: Then much people of the Iewes knew that hee was there: and they came, not for Jesus sake onely, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raysed from the dead.
12.10: The hie Priestes therefore consulted, that they might put Lazarus to death also,
12.11: Because that for his sake many of the Iewes went away, and beleeued in Jesus.
12.12: On the morowe a great multitude that were come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus should come to Hierusalem,
12.13: Took branches of palm trees, and went foorth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna, Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the Name of the Lord.
12.14: And Jesus found a yong ass, and sat thereon, as it is written,
12.15: Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy King cometh sitting on an asses colt.
12.16: But his disciples vnderstoode not these thinges at the first: but when Jesus was glorified, then remembred they, that these thinges were written of him, and that they had done these things unto him.
12.17: The people therefore that was with him, bare witness that hee called Lazarus out of the grave, and raised him from the dead.
12.18: Therefore met him the people also, because they heard that he had done this miracle.
12.19: And the Pharises said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? Behold, the world goeth after him.
12.20: Now there were certain Greekes among them that came up to worship at the feast.
12.21: And they came to Philippe, which was of Bethsaida in Galile, and desired him, saying, Syr, we would see that Jesus.
12.22: Philippe came and told Andrew: and again Andrew and Philippe told Jesus.
12.23: And Jesus answered them, saying, The hour is come, that the Sonne of man must bee glorified.
12.24: Verely, verely I say unto you, Except the wheat corn fall into the ground and die, it bideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth foorth much fruit.
12.25: He that loveth his life, shall lose it, and he that hateth his life in this world, shall keep it unto life eternal.
12.26: If any man serve me, let him follow me: for where I am, there shall also my servant be: and if any man serve me, him will my Father honour.
12.27: Now is my soul troubled: and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour: but therefore came I unto this hour.
12.28: Father, glorifie thy Name. Then came there a voyce from heaven, saying, I have both glorified it, and will glorifie it again.
12.29: Then said the people that stood by, and heard, that it was a thunder: other said, An Angel spake to him.
12.30: Jesus answered, and said, This voyce came not because of me, but for your sakes.
12.31: Now is the iudgement of this world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out.
12.32: And I, if I were lift up from the earth, will draw all men unto me.
12.33: Now this sayd he, signifying what death he should die.
12.34: The people answered him, We have heard out of the Law, that that Christ bideth for ever: and how sayest thou, that that Sonne of man must be lift up? Who is that Sonne of man?
12.35: Then Jesus sayd unto them, Yet a litle while is the light with you: walk while ye have that light, lest the darkenes come upon you: for hee that walketh in the dark, knoweth not whither he goeth.
12.36: While ye have that light, beleeue in that light, that ye may be the children of the light. These things spake Jesus, and departed, and hid himself from them.
12.37: And though he had done so many miracles before them, yet beleeued they not on him,
12.38: That the saying of Esaias the Prophet might be fulfilled, that he sayd, Lord, who beleeued our report? and to whom is the arm of the Lord reueiled?
12.39: Therefore could they not beleeue, because that Esaias saith again,
12.40: He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart, that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.
12.41: These things sayd Esaias when he saw his glory, and spake of him.
12.42: Neuertheles, even among the chief rulers, many beleeued in him: but because of the Pharises they did not confess him, least they should be cast out of the Synagogue.
12.43: For they loved the prayse of men, more then the prayse of God.
12.44: And Jesus cryed, and sayd, He that beleeueth in me, beleeueth not in me, but in him that sent me.
12.45: And he that seeth me, seeth him that sent me.
12.46: I am come a light into the world, that whosoever beleeueth in me, should not abide in darkenes.
12.47: And if any man hear my wordes, and beleeue not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.
12.48: He that refuseth me, and receiveth not my wordes, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I have spoken, it shall judge him in the last day.
12.49: For I have not spoken of my self: but the Father which sent me, hee gave me a commandement what I should say, and what I should speak.
12.50: And I know that his commandement is life everlasting: the thinges therefore that I speak, I speak them so as the Father sayde unto me.

13.1: Now before the feast of the Passeouer, when Jesus knew that his hour was come, that he should depart out of this world unto the Father, forasmuch as he loved his own which were in the world, unto the end he loved them.
13.2: And when supper was done (and that the devil had now put in the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simons sonne, to betray him)
13.3: Jesus knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he was come forth from God, and went to God,
13.4: He riseth from supper, and layeth aside his upper garments, and took a towel, and girded himself.
13.5: After that, hee powred water into a basen, and began to wash the disciples feet, and to wipe them with the towel, wherewith he was girded.
13.6: Then came he to Simon Peter, who sayd to him, Lord, doest thou wash my feet?
13.7: Jesus answered and sayd unto him, What I doe, thou knowest not now: but thou shalt know it hereafter.
13.8: Peter said unto him, Thou shalt never wash my feet. Jesus answered him, If I wash thee not, thou shalt have no part with me.
13.9: Simon Peter sayd unto him, Lord, not my feet onely, but also the hands and the head.
13.10: Jesus sayd to him, He that is washed, needeth not, save to wash his feet, but is clean every whit: and ye are clean, but not all.
13.11: For hee knew who should betray him: therefore sayd he, Ye are not all clean.
13.12: So after he had washed their feet, and had taken his garments, and was set down again, he sayd unto them, Know ye what I have done to you?
13.13: Ye call me Master, and Lord, and ye say well: for so am I.
13.14: If I then your Lord, and Master, have washed your feet, ye also ought to wash one an others feet.
13.15: For I have given you an example, that ye should doe, even as I have done to you.
13.16: Verely, verely I say unto you, The servant is not greater then his master, neither the ambassadour greater then he that sent him.
13.17: If ye know these things, blessed are ye, if ye doe them.
13.18: I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen: but it is that the Scripture might be fulfilled, He that eateth bread with me, hath lift up his heel against me.
13.19: From henceforth tell I you before it come, that when it is come to pass, ye might beleeue that I am he.
13.20: Verely, verely I say unto you, If I send any, he that receiveth him, receiveth me, and hee that receiveth me, receiveth him that sent me.
13.21: When Jesus had sayd these things, he was troubled in the Spirit, and testified, and said, Verely, verely I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.
13.22: Then the disciples looked one on another, doubting of whom he spake.
13.23: Now there was one of his disciples, which leaned on Jesus bosom, whom Jesus loved.
13.24: To him beckened therefore Simon Peter, that he should ask who it was of whom he spake.
13.25: He then, as he leaned on Jesus breast, said unto him, Lord, who is it?
13.26: Jesus answered, He it is, to whom I shall give a soppe, when I have dipt it: and hee wet a soppe, and gave it to Judas Iscariot, Simons sonne.
13.27: And after the soppe, Satan entred into him. Then sayd Jesus unto him, That thou doest, doe quickly.
13.28: But none of them that were at table, knew, for what cause he spake it unto him.
13.29: For some of them thought because Judas had the bag, that Jesus had sayd unto him, Buy those things that we have need of against ye feast: or that he should give some thing to the poor.
13.30: Assoone then as he had received the soppe, he went immediately out, and it was night.
13.31: When hee was gone out, Jesus sayd, Now is the Sonne of man glorified, and God is glorified in him.
13.32: If God be glorified in him, God shall also glorifie him in himself, and shall straightway glorifie him.
13.33: Litle children, yet a litle while am I with you: ye shall seek me, but as I sayde unto the Iewes, Whither I goe, can ye not come: also to you say I now,
13.34: A new commandement give I unto you, that ye love one another: as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
13.35: By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
13.36: Simon Peter said unto him, Lord, whither goest thou? Jesus answered him, Whither I goe, thou canst not follow me now: but thou shalt follow me afterward.
13.37: Peter sayd unto him, Lord, why can I not follow thee now? I will lay down my life for thy sake.
13.38: Jesus answered him, Wilt thou lay down thy life for my sake? Verely, verely I say unto thee, The cock shall not crow, till thou have denied me thrise.

14.1: Let not your heart be troubled: ye beleeue in God, beleeue also in me.
14.2: In my Fathers house are many dwelling places: if it were not so, I would have told you: I go to prepare a place for you.
14.3: And if I go to prepare a place for you, I wil come again, and receive you unto my self, that where I am, there may ye be also.
14.4: And whither I go, ye know, and the way ye know.
14.5: Thomas sayd unto him, Lord, we know not whither thou goest: how can we then know ye way?
14.6: Jesus sayd unto him, I am that Way, and that Trueth, and that Life. No man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
14.7: If ye had knowen mee, ye should have knowen my Father also: and from henceforth ye know him, and have seen him.
14.8: Philippe sayd unto him, Lord, shew us thy Father, and it sufficeth us.
14.9: Jesus sayd unto him, I have been so long time with you, and hast thou not knowen mee, Philippe? he that hath seen me, hath seen my Father: how then sayest thou, Shew us thy Father?
14.10: Beleeuest thou not, that I am in the Father, and the Father is in me? The wordes that I speak unto you, I speak not of my self: but the Father that dwelleth in me, he doeth the workes.
14.11: Beleeue me, that I am in the Father, and the Father is in me: at the least, beleeue me for the very workes sake.
14.12: Verely, verely I say unto you, he that beleeueth in me, the workes that I doe, hee shall doe also, and greater then these shall he doe: for I goe unto my Father.
14.13: And whatsoever ye ask in my Name, that will I doe, that the Father may be glorified in the Sonne.
14.14: If ye shall ask any thing in my Name, I will doe it.
14.15: If ye love me, keep my comandements,
14.16: And I wil pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever,
14.17: Even the Spirit of trueth, whom the world can not receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him: for he dwelleth with you, and shalbe in you.
14.18: I will not leave you fatherles: but I will come to you.
14.19: Yet a litle while, and the world shall see me no more, but ye shall see me: because I live, ye shall live also.
14.20: At that day shall ye know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.
14.21: He that hath my commandements, and keepeth them, is he that loveth me: and he that loveth me, shall be loved of my Father: and I will love him, and wil shew mine own self to him.
14.22: Judas sayd unto him (not Iscariot) Lord, what is the cause that thou wilt shew thy self unto us, and not unto the world?
14.23: Jesus answered, and sayd unto him, If any man love me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we wil come unto him, and wil dwell with him.
14.24: He that loveth me not, keepeth not my wordes, and the word which ye hear, is not mine, but the Fathers which sent me.
14.25: These things have I spoken unto you, being present with you.
14.26: But the Comforter, which is the holy Ghost, whom the Father wil send in my Name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, which I have told you.
14.27: Peace I leave with you: my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, nor fear.
14.28: Ye have heard how I said unto you, I goe away, and will come unto you. If ye loved me, ye would verely reioyce, because I said, I goe unto the Father: for the Father is greater then I.
14.29: And now have I spoken unto you, before it come, that when it is come to pass, ye might beleeue.
14.30: Hereafter will I not speak many things unto you: for the prince of this world cometh, and hath nought in me.
14.31: But it is that the world may know that I love my Father: and as the Father hath commanded me, so I doe. Arise, let us goe hence.

15.1: I Am that true vine, and my Father is that husband man.
15.2: Every branch that beareth not fruit in me, he taketh away: and every one that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.
15.3: Now are ye clean through the word, which I have spoken unto you.
15.4: Abide in me, and I in you: as the branch cannot bear fruit of it self, except it abide in the vine, no more can ye, except ye abide in me.
15.5: I am that vine: ye are the branches: he that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me can ye doe nothing.
15.6: If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and withereth: and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they burn.
15.7: If ye abide in me, and my wordes abide in you, ask what ye wil, and it shalbe done to you.
15.8: Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit, and be made my disciples.
15.9: As the father hath loved me, so have I loved you: continue in that my love.
15.10: If ye shall keep my commandements, ye shall abide in my love, as I have kept my Fathers commandements, and abide in his love.
15.11: These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
15.12: This is my commandement, that ye love one another, as I have loved you.
15.13: Greater love then this hath no man, when any man bestoweth his life for his friendes.
15.14: Ye are my friendes, if ye doe whatsoever I commaund you.
15.15: Henceforth call I you not servants: for the servant knoweth not what his master doeth: but I have called you friends: for all things that I have heard of my Father, have I made knowen to you.
15.16: Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordeined you, that ye goe and bring foorth fruit, and that your fruit remain, that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my Name, he may give it you.
15.17: These things commaund I you, that ye love one another.
15.18: If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before you.
15.19: If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of ye world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you.
15.20: Remember the word that I said unto you, The servant is not greater then his master. If they have persecuted me, they will persecute you also: if they have kept my word, they will also keep yours.
15.21: But all these things will they doe unto you for my Names sake, because they have not knowen him that sent me.
15.22: If I had not come and spoken unto them, they should not have had sinne: but now have they no cloke for their sinne.
15.23: He that hateth me, hateth my Father also.
15.24: If I had not done workes among them which none other man did, they had not had sinne: but now have they both seen, and have hated both me, and my Father.
15.25: But it is that the word might be fulfilled, that is written in their Law, They hated me without a cause.
15.26: But when that Comforter shall come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of trueth, which proceedeth of the Father, he shall testifie of me.
15.27: And ye shall witness also, because ye have been with me from the beginning.

16.1: These thinges have I said unto you, that ye should not be offended.
16.2: They shall excommunicate you: yea, the time shall come, that whosoever killeth you, will think that he doeth God service.
16.3: And these things will they doe unto you, because they have not knowen ye Father, nor me.
16.4: But these things have I told you, that when the hour shall come, ye might remember, that I told you them. And these things said I not unto you from ye beginning, because I was with you.
16.5: But now I go my way to him that sent me, and none of you asketh me, Whither goest thou?
16.6: But because I have said these thinges unto you, your hearts are full of sorowe.
16.7: Yet I tell you the trueth, It is expedient for you that I goe away: for if I goe not away, that Comforter will not come unto you: but if I depart, I will send him unto you.
16.8: And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sinne, and of righteousness, and of iudgement.
16.9: Of sinne, because they beleeued not in me:
16.10: Of righteousness, because I goe to my Father, and ye shall see me no more:
16.11: Of iudgement, because the prince of this world is judged.
16.12: I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.
16.13: Howbeit, when he is come which is the Spirit of trueth, he will lead you into all trueth: for he shall not speak of himself, but whatsoever he shall hear, shall he speak, and he will shew you the things to come.
16.14: He shall glorifie me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you.
16.15: All thinges that the Father hath, are mine: therefore said I, that he shall take of mine, and shew it unto you.
16.16: A litle while, and ye shall not see me: and again a litle while, and ye shall see me: for I goe to the Father.
16.17: Then said some of his disciples among them selves, What is this that he saieth unto us, A litle while, and ye shall not see me, and again, a litle while, and ye shall see me, and, For I goe to the Father.
16.18: They said therefore, What is this that he saith, A litle while? we know not what he sayeth.
