16.19: Now Jesus knew that they would ask him, and said unto them, Doe ye enquire among your selves, of that I said, A litle while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a litle while, and yee shall see me?
16.20: Verely, verely I say unto you, that ye shall weep and lament, and the world shall reioyce: and ye shall sorowe, but your sorowe shalbe turned to ioye.
16.21: A woman when she traueileth, hath sorowe, because her hour is come: but assoone as she is delivered of the child, she remembreth no more the anguish, for joy that a man is borne into the world.
16.22: And ye now therefore are in sorowe: but I will see you again, and your hearts shall reioyce, and your joy shall no man take from you.
16.23: And in that day shall ye ask me nothing. Verely, verely I say unto you, whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my Name, he will give it you.
16.24: Hitherto have ye asked nothing in my Name: ask, and ye shall receive, that your ioye may be full.
16.25: These things have I spoken unto you in parables: but the time will come, when I shall no more speak to you in parables: but I shall shew you plainely of the Father.
16.26: At that day shall ye ask in my Name, and I say not unto you, that I will pray unto the Father for you:
16.27: For the Father himself loveth you, because ye have loved me, and have beleeued that I came out from God.
16.28: I am come out from the Father, and came into the world: again I leave the world, and goe to the Father.
16.29: His disciples said unto him, Loe, now speakest thou plainely, and thou speakest no parable.
16.30: Now know wee that thou knowest all things, and needest not that any man should ask thee. By this we beleeue, that thou art come out from God.
16.31: Jesus answered them, Doe you beleeue now?
16.32: Behold, the hour cometh, and is already come, that ye shalbe scattered every man into his own, and shall leave me alone: but I am not alone: for the Father is with me.
16.33: These thinges have I spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace: in the world ye shall have affliction, but be of good comfort: I have overcome the world.

17.1: These things spake Jesus, and lift up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, that hour is come: glorifie thy Sonne, that thy Sonne also may glorifie thee,
17.2: As thou hast given him power over all flesh, that he should give eternal life to all them that thou hast given him.
17.3: And this is life eternal, that they know thee to be the onely very God, and whom thou hast sent, Jesus Christ.
17.4: I have glorified thee on the earth: I have finished the work which thou gavest me to doe.
17.5: And now glorifie me, thou Father, with thine own self, with the glorie which I had with thee before the world was.
17.6: I have declared thy Name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me, and they have kept thy word.
17.7: Now they know that all things whatsoever thou hast given me, are of thee.
17.8: For I have given unto them the wordes which thou gavest me, and they have received them, and have knowen surely that I came out from thee, and have beleeued that thou hast sent me.
17.9: I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me: for they are thine.
17.10: And al mine are thine, and thine are mine, and I am glorified in them.
17.11: And now am I no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep them in thy Name, even them whom thou hast given mee, that they may bee one, as we are.
17.12: While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy Name: those that thou gavest me, have I kept, and none of them is lost, but the child of perdition, that the Scripture might be fulfilled.
17.13: And now come I to thee, and these things speak I in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves.
17.14: I have given them thy word, and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, as I am not of the world.
17.15: I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou keep them from evil.
17.16: They are not of the world, as I am not of the world.
17.17: Sanctifie them with thy trueth: thy word is trueth.
17.18: As thou diddest send me into the world, so have I sent them into the world.
17.19: And for their sakes sanctifie I my self, that they also may bee sanctified through the trueth.
17.20: I praie not for these alone, but for them also which shall beleeue in mee, through their woorde,
17.21: That they all may bee one, as thou, O Father, art in me, and I in thee: even that they may be also one in us, that the world may beleeue that thou hast sent me.
17.22: And the glory that thou gavest me, I have given them, that they may be one, as we are one,
17.23: I in them, and thou in mee, that they may be made perfect in one, and that the world may know that thou hast sent mee, and hast loved them, as thou hast loved me.
17.24: Father, I will that they which thou hast given me, be with me even where I am, that they may behold that my glorie, which thou hast given mee: for thou lovedst me before the foundation of the world.
17.25: O righteous Father, the world also hath not knowen thee, but I have knowen thee, and these have knowen, that thou hast sent me.
17.26: And I have declared unto the thy Name, and will declare it, that the love wherewith thou hast loved me, may be in them, and I in them.

18.1: When Jesus had spoken these things, hee went foorth with his disciples over the brook Cedron, where was a garden, into the which he entred, and his disciples.
18.2: And Judas which betraied him, knew also the place: for Jesus oft times resorted thither with his disciples.
18.3: Judas then, after hee had received a band of men and officers of the high Priests, and of the Pharises, came thither with lanternes and torches, and weapons.
18.4: Then Jesus, knowing all things that should come unto him, went foorth and said unto them, Whom seek yee?
18.5: They answered him, Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus sayde unto them, I am hee. Now Judas also which betraied him, stood with them.
18.6: Assoone then as hee had said unto them, I am hee, they went away backewardes, and fell to the ground.
18.7: Then he asked them again, Whom seek yee? And they sayd, Jesus of Nazareth.
18.8: Jesus answered, I said unto you, that I am he: therefore if ye seek me, let these go their way.
18.9: This was that the word might be fulfilled which hee spake, Of them which thou gavest me, have I lost none.
18.10: Then Simon Peter having a sword, drew it, and smote the hie Priests servant, and cut off his right ear. Now the servants name was Malchus.
18.11: Then sayde Jesus unto Peter, Put up thy sword into the sheath: shall I not drink of the cuppe which my Father hath given me?
18.12: Then the band and the captain, and the officers of the Iewes took Jesus, and bound him,
18.13: And led him away to Annas first (for he was father in law to Caiaphas, which was the hie Priest that same yeere)
18.14: And Caiaphas was he, that gave counsel to the Iewes, that it was expedient that one man should die for the people.
18.15: Now Simon Peter folowed Jesus, and another disciple, and that disciple was knowen of the hie Priest: therefore he went in with Jesus into the hall of the hie Priest:
18.16: But Peter stood at the door without. Then went out the other disciple which was knowen unto the hie Priest, and spake to her that kept the door, and brought in Peter.
18.17: Then said the maid that kept the door, unto Peter, Art not thou also one of this mans disciples? He sayd, I am not.
18.18: And the servants and officers stood there, which had made a fire of coles: for it was cold, and they warmed themselves. And Peter also stood among them, and warmed himself.
18.19: (The hie Priest then asked Jesus of his disciples, and of his doctrine.
18.20: Jesus answered him, I spake openly to the world: I ever taught in the Synagogue and in the Temple, whither the Iewes resort continually, and in secret have I sayde nothing.
18.21: Why askest thou mee? ask them which heard mee what I sayde unto them: behold, they know what I sayd.
18.22: When he had spoken these thinges, one of the officers which stood by, smote Jesus with his rod, saying, Answerest thou the hie Priest so?
18.23: Jesus answered him, If I have evil spoken, bear witnes of the evil: but if I have well spoken, why smitest thou me?
18.24: Now Annas had sent him bound unto Caiaphas the hie Priest)
18.25: And Simon Peter stood and warmed himself, and they said unto him, Art not thou also of his disciples? He denied it, and said, I am not.
18.26: One of the seruaunts of the hie Priest, his cousin whose ear Peter smote off, said, Did not I see thee in the garden with him?
18.27: Peter then denied again, and immediatly the cock crew.
18.28: Then led they Jesus from Caiaphas into the common hall. Now it was morning, and they themselves went not into the common hall, least they should be defiled, but that they might eat the Passeouer.
18.29: Pilate then went out unto them, and said, What accusation bring yee against this man?
18.30: They answered, and said unto him, If hee were not an evil doer, we would not have delivered him unto thee.
18.31: Then sayde Pilate unto them, Take yee him, and judge him after your own Law. Then the Iewes sayde unto him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death.
18.32: It was that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled which he spake, signifying what death he should die.
18.33: So Pilate entred into the common hall again, and called Jesus, and sayde unto him, Art thou the king of the Iewes?
18.34: Jesus answered him, Saiest thou that of thy self, or did other tell it thee of me?
18.35: Pilate answered, Am I a Iewe? Thine own nation, and the hie Priestes have delivered thee unto me. What hast thou done?
18.36: Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, my servants would surely fight, that I should not be delivered to the Iewes: but now is my kingdom not from hence.
18.37: Pilate then said unto him, Art thou a King then? Jesus answered, Thou sayest that I am a King: for this cause am I borne, and for this cause came I into the world, that I should bear witnes unto the trueth: every one that is of the trueth, heareth my voyce.
18.38: Pilate said unto him, What is trueth? And when he had said that, hee went out again unto the Iewes, and said unto them, I find in him no cause at all.
18.39: But you have a custom, that I should deliver you one loose at the Passeouer: will yee then that I loose unto you the King of ye Iewes?
18.40: Then cried they all again, saying, Not him, but Barabbas: now this Barabbas was a murtherer.

19.1: Then Pilate took Jesus and scourged him.
19.2: And the souldiers platted a crown of thornes, and put it on his head, and they put on him a purple garment,
19.3: And said, Hail, King of the Iewes. And they smote him with their roddes.
19.4: Then Pilate went foorth again, and said unto them, Behold, I bring him forth to you, that ye may know, that I find no fault in him at all.
19.5: Then came Jesus foorth wearing a crown of thornes, and a purple garment. And Pilate said unto them, Behold the man.
19.6: Then when the hie Priests and officers saw him, they cried, saying, Crucifie, crucifie him. Pilate said unto them, Take yee him and crucifie him: for I find no fault in him.
19.7: The Iewes answered him, We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Sonne of God.
19.8: When Pilate then heard that woorde, he was the more afraid,
19.9: And went again into the common hall, and said unto Jesus, Whence art thou? But Jesus gave him none answer.
19.10: Then said Pilate unto him, Speakest thou not unto me? Knowest thou not that I have power to crucifie thee, and have power to loose thee?
19.11: Jesus answered, Thou couldest have no power at all against me, except it were given thee from above: therefore he that delivered me unto thee, hath the greater sinne.
19.12: From thence foorth Pilate sought to loose him, but the Iewes cried, saying, If thou deliver him, thou art not Cesars friend: for whosoever maketh himself a King, speaketh against Cesar.
19.13: When Pilate heard this woorde, hee brought Jesus foorth, and sat down in the iudgement seat in a place called the Pavement, and in Hebrew, Gabbatha.
19.14: And it was the Preparation of the Passeouer, and about the sixt hour: and hee sayde unto the Iewes, Behold your King.
19.15: But they cried, Away with him, away with him, crucifie him. Pilate sayde unto them, Shall I crucifie your King? The high Priestes answered, We have no King but Cesar.
19.16: Then delivered he him unto them, to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away.
19.17: And he bare his own cross, and came into a place named of dead mens Skulles, which is called in Hebrew, Golgotha:
19.18: Where they crucified him, and two other with him, on either side one, and Jesus in the middes.
19.19: And Pilate wrote also a title, and put it on the cross, and it was written, JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWES.
19.20: This title then read many of the Iewes: for the place where Jesus was crucified, was neere to the citie: and it was written in Hebrew, Greek and Latin.
19.21: Then said the hie Priests of the Iewes to Pilate, Write not, The King of the Iewes, but that he sayd, I am King of the Iewes.
19.22: Pilate answered, What I have written, I have written.
19.23: Then the souldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments (and made four partes, to every souldier a part) and his coat: and the coat was without seam woven from the toppe throughout.
19.24: Therefore they sayde one to another, Let us not deuide it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be. This was that the Scripture might be fulfilled, which sayth, They parted my garments among them, and on my coat did cast lots. So the souldiers did these things in deed.
19.25: Then stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mothers sister, Marie the wife of Cleopas, and Marie Magdalene.
19.26: And when Jesus saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he said unto his mother, Woman, behold thy sonne.
19.27: Then said he to the disciple, Behold thy mother: and from that hour, the disciple took her home unto him.
19.28: After, when Jesus knew that all things were performed, that the Scripture might be fulfilled, he said, I thirst.
19.29: And there was set a vessell full of vineger: and they filled a spondge with vineger: and put it about an Hyssop stalk, and put it to his mouth.
19.30: Now when Jesus had received of the vineger, he said, It is finished, and bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.
19.31: The Iewes then (because it was the Preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the Sabbath day: for that Sabbath was an hie day) besought Pilate that their legges might be broken, and that they might be taken down.
19.32: Then came the souldiers and brake the legges of the first, and of the other, which was crucified with Jesus.
19.33: But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead alreadie, they brake not his legges.
19.34: But one of the souldiers with a spear pearced his side, and foorthwith came there out blood and water.
19.35: And he that saw it, bare record, and his record is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye might beleeue it.
19.36: For these things were done, that the Scripture should be fulfilled, Not a bone of him shalbe broken.
19.37: And again an other Scripture saith, They shall see him whom they have thrust through.
19.38: And after these things, Joseph of Arimathea (who was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Iewes) besought Pilate that he might take down the bodie of Jesus. And Pilate gave him licence. He came then and took Jesus body.
19.39: And there came also Nicodemus (which first came to Jesus by night) and brought of myrrh and aloes mingled together about an hundreth pound.
19.40: Then took they the body of Jesus, and wrapped it in linen clothes with the odours, as the maner of the Iewes is to burie.
19.41: And in that place where Jesus was crucified, was a garden, and in the garden a new sepulchre, wherein was never man yet laid.
19.42: There then laid they Jesus, because of the Iewes Preparation day, for the sepulchre was neere.

20.1: Now the first day of the week came Marie Magdalene, early when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre, and saw the stone taken away from the tomb.
20.2: Then she ranne, and came to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and said unto them, They have taken away the Lord out of the sepulchre, and we know not where they have laid him.
20.3: Peter therefore went forth, and the other disciple, and they came unto the sepulchre.
20.4: So they ranne both together, but the other disciple did outrunne Peter, and came first to the sepulchre.
20.5: And he stouped down, and saw the linen clothes lying: yet went he not in.
20.6: Then came Simon Peter following him, and went into the sepulchre, and saw the linen clothes lye,
20.7: And the kerchiefe that was upon his head, not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by it self.
20.8: Then went in also the other disciple, which came first to the sepulchre, and he saw it, and beleeued.
20.9: For as yet they knew not the Scripture, That he must rise again from the dead.
20.10: And the disciples went away again unto their own home.
20.11: But Marie stood without at the sepulchre weeping: and as she wept, she bowed her self into the sepulchre,
20.12: And saw two Angels in white, sitting, the one at the head, and the other at the feet, where the body of Jesus had laien.
20.13: And they said unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? She said unto them, They have taken away my Lord, and I know not where they have laid him.
20.14: When she had thus said, she turned her self back, and saw Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus.
20.15: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She supposing that he had been the gardener, said unto him, Sir, if thou hast borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.
20.16: Jesus saith unto her, Marie. She turned her self, and said unto him, Rabboni, which is to say, Master.
20.17: Jesus saith unto her, Touch me not: for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but goe to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and to your Father, and to my God, and your God.
20.18: Marie Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and that he had spoken these things unto her.
20.19: The same day then at night, which was the first day of the week, and when the doores were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Iewes, came Jesus and stood in the middes, and said to them, Peace be unto you.
20.20: And when he had so said, he shewed unto them his handes, and his side. Then were the disciples glad when they had seen the Lord.
20.21: Then said Jesus to them again, Peace be unto you: as my Father sent me, so send I you.
20.22: And when he had said that, he breathed on them, and said unto them, Receive the holy Ghost.
20.23: Whosoeuers sinnes ye remit, they are remitted unto them: and whosoeuers sinnes ye reteine, they are reteined.
20.24: But Thomas one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
20.25: The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord: but he said unto them, Except I see in his handes the print of the nailes, and put my finger into the print of the nailes, and put mine hand into his side, I will not beleeue it.
20.26: And eight dayes after, again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them. Then came Jesus, when the doores were shut, and stood in the middes, and said, Peace be unto you.
20.27: After said he to Thomas, Put thy finger here, and see mine hands, and put forth thine hand, and put it into my side, and be not faithless, but faithful.
20.28: Then Thomas answered, and said unto him, Thou art my Lord, and my God.
20.29: Jesus said unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou beleeuest: blessed are they that have not seen, and have beleeued.
20.30: And many other signes also did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book.
20.31: But these things are written, that ye might beleeue, that Jesus is that Christ that Sonne of God, and that in beleeuing ye might have life through his Name.

21.1: After these things, Jesus shewed himself again to his disciples at the sea of Tiberias: and thus shewed he himself:
21.2: There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas, which is called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galile, and the sonnes of Zebedeus, and two other of his disciples.
21.3: Simon Peter said unto them, I go a fishing. They said unto him, We also will goe with thee. They went their way and entred into a ship straightway, and that night caught they nothing.
21.4: But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: nevertheless the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.
21.5: Jesus then said unto them, Syrs, have ye any meat? They answered him, No.
21.6: Then he said unto them, Cast out the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find. So they cast out, and they were not able at all to draw it, for the multitude of fishes.
21.7: Therefore said the disciple whom Jesus loved, unto Peter, It is the Lord. When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girded his coat to him (for he was naked) and cast himself into the sea.
21.8: But the other disciples came by shippe (for they were not far from land, but about two hundreth cubites) and they drew the net with fishes.
21.9: Assoone then as they were come to land, they saw hoate coales, and fish laid thereon, and bread.
21.10: Jesus said unto them, Bring of the fishes, which ye have now caught.
21.11: Simon Peter stepped foorth and drew the net to land, full of great fishes, an hundreth, fiftie and three: and albeit there were so many, yet was not the net broken.
21.12: Jesus said unto them, Come, and dine. And none of the disciples durst ask him, Who art thou? seeing they knew that he was the Lord.
21.13: Jesus then came and took bread, and gave them, and fish likewise.
21.14: This is now the third time that Jesus shewed himself to his disciples, after that he was risen again from the dead.
21.15: So when they had dined, Jesus said to Simon Peter, Simon the sonne of Jona, lovest thou me more then these? He said unto him, Yea Lord, thou knowest that I love thee. He said unto him, Feed my lambes.
21.16: He said to him again the second time, Simon the sonne of Jona, lovest thou me? He said unto him, Yea Lord, thou knowest that I love thee. He said unto him, Feed my sheep.
21.17: He said unto him the third time, Simon the sonne of Jona, lovest thou me? Peter was sorie because he said to him the third time, Lovest thou me? and said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things: thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus said unto him, Feed my sheep.
21.18: Verely, verely I say unto thee, When thou wast yong, thou girdedst thy self, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch foorth thine hands, and another shall gird thee, and lead thee whither thou wouldest not.
21.19: And this spake he signifying by what death he should glorifie God. And when he had said this, he said to him, Folowe me.
21.20: Then Peter turned about, and saw the disciple whom JESUS loved, folowing, which had also leaned on his breast at supper, and had said, Lord, which is he that betrayeth thee?
21.21: When Peter therefore saw him, he said to Jesus, Lord, what shall this man doe?
21.22: Jesus said unto him, If I will that he tarie till I come, what is it to thee? follow thou me.
21.23: Then went this word abroad among the brethren, that this disciple should not die. Yet Jesus said not to him, He shall not die: but if I will that he tarie till I come, what is it to thee?
21.24: This is that disciple, which testifieth of these things, and wrote these things, and we know that his testimonie is true.
21.25: Now there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which if they should be written every one, I suppose the world could not conteine the bookes that should be written, Amen.

43:1:1: This word (With) putteth out the distinction of persons to us.
This word (Word) is the first in order in the sentence, and is that which the learned call (Subjectum:) and this word (God) is the latter in order, and the same which the learned call (Predicatum.)
The Son of God is of one, and the selfsame eternity or everlastingness, and of one and the selfsame essence or nature, with the Father.

From his beginning, as the Evangelist saith, 1 John 1:1, as though he said, that the world began not then to have his being, when God began to make all that was made: for the word was even then when all things that were made, began to be made, and therefore he was before the beginning of all things.

This word, That, pointeth out unto us a peculiar and choice thing above all other, and putteth a difference between this Word, which is the Son of God, and the Laws of God, which otherwise also are called the word of God.
43:1:3: Paul expoundeth this place, Col. 1:15 and 16.
Of all those things which were made, nothing was made without him.

The son of God declareth that same his everlasting Godhead, both by the creating of all things, and also by the preserving of them, and especially by the excellent gifts of reason and understanding, wherewith he that beautified man above all other creatures.
That is, as the Father did work, so did the Son work with him: for he was fellow worker with him.
43:1:4: That is, by him: and it is spoken after the manner of the Hebrews, meaning thereby that by his force and working power all life cometh to the world.
That force of reason and understanding, which is kindled in our minds to acknowledge him, the author of so great a benefit.
To wit, even then, when all things are made by him, for else he would have said, Life is in him, and not life was.
43:1:5: They could not perceive nor reach unto it, to receive any light of it, no, they did not so much as acknowledge him.
The light of men is turned into darkness, but yet so that there is clearness enough to make them without excuse.
43:1:6: There is another more full manifestation of the Son of God, to the consideration whereof men are in good time stirred up, even by John’s voice, who is as it were the herald of Christ.
43:1:8: That light which we spake of, to wit, Christ, who only can lighten our darkness.
43:1:9: When as the Son of God saw, that man did not acknowledge him by his works, although they were endued with understanding (which he had given to them all) he exhibited himself unto his people to be seen of them with their corporal eyes: yet neither so did they acknowledge him, nor receive him.
Who only and properly deserveth to be called the light, for he shineth of himself and borroweth light of none.
43:1:10: That person of the Word, was made manifest even at that time when the world was made.
43:1:11: The Word showed himself again, when he came in the flesh.
43:1:12: The Son being shut out of the most of his people, and acknowledged but of a few, doth regenerate them by his own virtue and power, and receiveth them into that honor which is common to all the children of God, that is to be the sons of God.
He vouchsafed to give them this prerogative to take them to be his children.
43:1:13: Of that gross and corrupt nature of man, which is throughout the Scriptures set as enemy to the Spirit.
43:1:14: The glory which he speaketh of here, is that manifestation of Christ’s majesty, which was as it were laid open before our eyes when the Son of God appeared in flesh.

This word (as) doth not in this place betoken a likeness, but the truth of the matter, for his meaning is this, that we saw such a glory, as beseemed and was meet for the true and only begotten Son of God, who is Lord and King over all the world.
He was not only a partaker of grace and truth, but was full of the very substance of grace and truth.

That Son, who is God from everlasting, took upon him man’s nature, that one and the selfsame might be both God and man, which manifestly appeared to many witnesses, that saw him amongst whom he was conversant, and unto whom by sure and undoubted arguments he showed both his natures.
That is, man: so that the part is taken for the whole, by the figure Synecdoche: for he took upon him all our whole nature, that is to say, a true body, and a true soul.

For a season, and when that was ended, he went up into heaven: for the word which he useth, is taken from tents: and yet notwithstanding, his absence from us in body is not such, but that he is always present with us, though not in flesh, yet by the virtue of his Spirit.
43:1:15: That is, He before whom I am sent to prepare him the way: so that these words are referred to the time of his calling, and not of his age, for John was six months older than he.
John is a faithful witness of the excellency of Christ.

This sentence hath in it a turning of the reason as we call it, as who would say, a setting of that first which should be last, and that last which should be first: for in plain speech this it is: He that cometh after me, is better than I am, for he was before me. The like kind of turning the reason we find in Luke 7:47: many sins are forgiven her, because she loved much, which is thus much to say, she loved much, because many sins are forgiven her.
43:1:16: That is grace upon grace, as a man would say graces heaped one upon another.
Christ is the most plentiful fountain of all goodness, but then he poured out his gifts most bountifully, when as he exhibited and showed himself to the world.
43:1:18: Who is nearest to his Father, not only in respect of his love towards him, but by the bond of nature, and for that union or oneness that is between them, whereby the Father and the Son are one.

Revealed him, and showed him unto us, whereas before he was hid under the shadows of the Law, so that the quickness of the sight of our minds was not able to perceive him: for whosoever seeth him, seeth the Father also.
That true knowledge of God proceedeth only from Jesus Christ.
43:1:19: John is neither the Messiah, nor like to any of the other Prophets, but is the herald of Christ, who is now present.
43:1:20: He did acknowledge him, and spake of him plainly and openly.

This repeating of the one and the selfsame thing, though in divers words, is used much of the Hebrews, and it hath great force: for they used to speak one thing twice, to set it out more certainly and plainly.
43:1:21: The Jews thought that Elijah should come again before the days of Messiah, and they took the ground of that their opinion out of Mal. 4:5, which place is to be understood of John, Matt. 11:14. And yet John denieth that he is Elijah, answering them indeed according as they meant.

They inquire of some great Prophet, and not of Christ, for John denied before, that he is Christ, for they thought that some great Prophet should be sent like unto Moses, wresting to that purpose that place of Deut. 18:15, which is to be understood of all the company of the Prophets and ministers, which have been and shall be to the end, and especially of Christ, who is the head of all Prophets.
43:1:24: Christ is the author of baptism, and not John: and therefore the force thereof consisteth not in John, who is the minister, but wholly in Christ the Lord.
43:1:25: Hereby we may prove that the Jews knew there should be some change in religion under Messiah.
43:1:26: Whom all the world seeth not, and is even amongst you.
43:1:27: Matt. 3:11; Mark 1:7; Luke 3:16; Acts 1:5; Acts 11:16; Acts 19:4
43:1:29: The body and truth of all the sacrifices of the Law, to make satisfaction for the sin of the world, is in Christ.
That is, that root of sins, to wit, our corruption, and so consequently, the fruits of sin, which are commonly called in the plural number sins.
This word of the present time signifieth a continual act, for the Lamb hath this virtue proper unto him, and forever, to take away the sins of the world.

This word (That) which is added, hath great force in it, not only to set forth the worthiness of Christ, and so to separate him from the Lamb which was a figure of him, and from all other sacrifices of the Law, but also to bring into our mind the Prophecies of Isaiah and others.
43:1:31: I never knew him by face before.
43:1:32: Christ is proved to be the Son of God, by the coming down of the holy Ghost, by the Father’s voice, and by John’s testimony.
43:1:34: This word (That) pointeth out unto us some excellent thing, and maketh a difference between Christ and others, whom Moses and the Prophets commonly call the sons of God, or the sons of the most high.
43:1:35: John gathered disciples, not to himself, but to Christ.
43:1:36: Christ is set before us to follow not as a vain shadow, but as our Mediator.
43:1:37: In this first gathering of the disciples we have shown unto us, that the beginning of salvation is from God, who calleth us unto his Son by the ministry of his servants: whom (so preventing us) we must also hear, and follow him home, that being instructed by him, we may also instruct others.
43:1:41: That is, anointed, and King after the manner of the Jewish people.
43:1:45: The good endeavors even of the unlearned, God doth so allow, that he maketh them masters to the learned.
43:1:46: We must especially take heed of false presumptions, which shut up against us the entrance to Christ.
43:1:47: Simple uprightness discerneth the true Israelites from the false.
43:1:48: The end of miracles is to set before us Christ the Almighty, and also the only author of our salvation, that we may apprehend him by faith.
43:1:51: By these words the power of God is signified which should appear in his ministry by the angels serving him as the head of the Church.
43:2:1: After the talk which he had with Nathanael, or after that he departured from John, or after that he came into Galilee.

Christ declaring openly in an assembly by a notable miracle, that he hath power over the nature of things, to feed man’s body, leadeth the minds of all men, to his spiritual and saving virtue and power.
43:2:3: Christ is careful enough of our salvation, and therefore hath no need of others to put him in mind of it.
43:2:6: These were vessels appointed for water, wherein they washed themselves.
Every firkin contained an hundred pounds, at twelve ounces the pound: Whereby we gather that Christ helped them with a thousand and eight hundred pounds of wine.
43:2:10: Word for word, are drunken. Now this speech, to be drunken, is not always taken in evil part in the Hebrew tongue, but signifieth sometime such store, and plentiful use of wine, as doth not pass measure, as Gen. 43:34.
43:2:13: Christ being made subject to the Law for us, satisfieth the Law of the Passover.
43:2:14: Christ being ordained to purge the Church, doth with great zeal begin his office both of Priest and Prophet.
43:2:17: Zeal in this place is taken for a wrathful indignation and displeasure of the mind, conceived of some naughty and evil dealing towards them whom we love well.
43:2:18: Against them which so bind God to an ordinary calling which they themselves most shamefully abuse, that they will not admit an extraordinary, which God confirmeth from heaven, (and they although in vain would have it extinguished) unless it be sealed with outward and bodily miracles.
With what miracle dost thou confirm it, that we may see that heavenly power and virtue, which giveth thee authority to speak and do thus?
43:2:24: It is not good crediting them, which stand only upon miracles.
43:2:25: Christ is the searcher of hearts, and therefore true God.
43:3:1: A man of great estimation, and a ruler amongst the Jews.
There are none sometimes more unlearned, than the learned: but as well the learned as the unlearned must desire wisdom of Christ only.
43:3:2: We know that thou art sent from God to teach us.
But he in whom some part of the excellency of God appeareth. And if Nicodemus had known Christ aright, he would not only have said that God was with him, but in him: as Paul doth, 2 Cor. 1:19.

That is, go in, or enter, as he expounded himself afterward, verse 5.
The Church: for Christ showeth in this place, how we come to be citizens, and to have ought to do in the city of God.
43:3:4: How can I that am old, be born again? for he answereth, as if Christ’s words belonged to none but to him.
43:3:6: That is, fleshly, to wit, wholly unclean and under the wrath of God: and therefore this word (Flesh) signifieth the corrupt nature of man: contrary to which is the Spirit, that is, the man ingrafted into Christ through the grace of the holy Ghost, whose nature is everlasting and immortal, though the strife of the flesh remaineth.
43:3:8: With free and wandering blasts, as it listeth.
43:3:9: The secret mystery of our regeneration which cannot be comprehended by man’s capacity, is perceived by faith, and that in Christ only, because that he is both God on earth, and man in heaven, that is to say, in such sort man, that he is God also, and therefore almighty: and in such sort God, that he is man also, and therefore his power is manifest unto us.
43:3:11: You handle doubtful things, and such as you have no certain author for, and yet men believe you: but I teach those things that are of a truth and well known, and you believe me not.
43:3:13: That is, hath any spiritual light and understanding, or ever had, but only that Son of God, which came down to us.

That which is proper to the divinity of Christ, is here spoken of whole Christ, to give us to understand that he is but one person, wherein two natures are united, and this kind of speech men call, the communicating of proprieties.
Only Christ can teach us heavenly things for no man ascendeth, etc.

Whereas he is said to have come down from heaven, that must be understood of his Godhead, and of the manner of his conception: for Christ’s birth upon the earth was heavenly, and not earthly, for he was conceived by the holy Ghost.
43:3:16: Nothing else but the free love of the Father, is the beginning of our salvation, and Christ is he in whom our righteousness and salvation is resident: and faith is the instrument or mean whereby we apprehend it, and life everlasting is that which is set before us to apprehend.

It is not all one to believe in a thing, and to believe of a thing, for we may not believe (in anything) save only in God, but we may believe (of anything) whatsoever, this saith Nazianzene in his oration of the Spirit.
43:3:17: Not only the people of the Jews, but whosoever shall believe in him.
That is, to be the cause of the condemning of the world, for indeed sins are the cause of death, but Christ shall judge the quick and the dead.
Not Christ, but the despising of Christ doth condemn.
43:3:19: Only wickedness is the cause, why men refuse the light that is offered them.
That is, the cause of condemnation, which sticketh fast in men, unless through God’s great benefit they be delivered from it.
43:3:21: That is, he that leadeth an honest life, and void of all craft and deceit.
That is, with God, God as it were going before.

43:3:27: What mean you to go about to better my state? this is every man’s lot and portion that they cannot better themselves one iota.

Is nothing else but man, a piece of work and of the slime of the earth.
43:3:32: What he knoweth fully and perfectly.

43:4:6: Even as he was weary, or because he was weary.
43:4:9: There is no familiarity nor friendship, between the Jews and the Samaritans.
43:4:10: By this word (That) we are given to understand, that Christ speaketh of some excellent gift, that is to say, even of himself, whom his Father offered to this woman.

This everlasting water, that is to say, the exceeding love of God, is called living, or of life, to make a difference between it, and the water that should be drawn out of a well: and these metaphors are very much used of the Jews, Jer. 2:13; Joel 3:18; Zech. 13:11.
43:4:20: All the religion of superstitious people, standeth for the most part, upon two pillars, but very weak, that is to say upon the examples of the fathers perverted, and a foolish opinion of outward things: against which errors we have to set the word and nature of God.

The name of this mountain is Gerizim, whereupon Sanabaletta the Cushite built a Temple by Alexander of Macedonia’s leave, after the victory of Issica, and made there Manasses his son-in-law high priest, Josephus, book 11.
43:4:23: This word (Spirit) is to be taken here, as it is set against that commandment, which is called carnal, Heb. 7:16, as the commandment is considered in itself: and so he speaketh of (Truth) not as we set it against a lie, but as we take it in respect of the outward ceremonies of the Law: which did only shadow that which Christ performed indeed.
43:4:24: By the word (Spirit) he meaneth the nature of the Godhead, and not the third person in the Trinity.

43:4:39: The Samaritans do most joyfully embrace that which the Jews most stubbornly rejected.
43:4:43: The despisers of Christ deprive themselves of his benefit: yet Christ prepareth a place for himself.

Into the towns and villages of Galilee: for he would not make abode in his country of Nazareth, because they despised him, and where (as the other Evangelists write) the efficacy of his benefits was hindered through their marvelous stiffneckedness.
43:4:46: Some of Herod’s courtiers, for though Herod was not a king, but a Tetrarch, yet the lofty name only except, he was a king, or at least the people called him a king.
Although Christ be absent in body, yet he worketh mightily in the believers by his word.

There is no disease so old, which Christ cannot heal.
Whereof cattle drank, and used to be plunged in; whereof there could not be but great store at Jerusalem.
43:5:10: True religion is no more cruelly assaulted by any means, than by the pretence of religion itself.

43:5:18: That is, his only and no man’s else, which they gather by that, that he saith, (And I work) applying this word (work) to himself, which is proper to God, and therefore maketh himself equal to God.
43:5:19: This must be understood of Christ’s person, which consisteth of two natures, and not simply of his Godhead: so then he saith that his Father moveth and governeth him in all things, but yet notwithstanding, when he saith he worketh with his Father, he voucheth his Godhead.
Not only without his Father’s authority, but also without his mighty working and power.

In like sort, jointly and together. Not for that the Father doeth some things, and then the son worketh after him, and doeth the like, but because the might and power of the Father and the Son do work equally and jointly together.
43:5:21: The Father maketh no man partaker of everlasting life, but in Christ, in whom only also he is truly worshipped.
43:5:22: These words are not so to be taken, as though they simply denied that God governeth the world, but as the Jews imagined it, which separate the Father from the Son, whereas indeed, the Father doth not govern the world but only in the person of his Son, being made manifest in the flesh: so saith he afterward, verse 30, that he came not to do his own will: that his doctrine is not his own, John 7:16, that the blind man and his parents sinned not, etc., John 9:3.
This word (judgeth) is taken by the figure Synecdoche, for all government.
43:5:24: The Father is not worshipped but by his Son’s word apprehended by faith, which is the only way that leadeth to eternal life.
43:5:25: We are all dead in sin and cannot be quickened by any other means, than by the word of Christ apprehended by faith.

That is, high and sovereign power to rule and govern all things, insomuch that he hath power of life and death.
43:5:28: All shall appear before the judgment seat of Christ at length to be judged.
43:5:29: To that resurrection which had life everlasting following it: against which is set the resurrection of condemnation: that is, which condemnation followeth.
Faith and infidelity shall be judged by their fruits.
43:5:30: As my father directeth me, who dwelleth in me.
The father is the author and approver of all things which Christ doeth.
43:5:31: Faithful, that is, worthy to be credited, see John 8:14.
43:5:33: Christ is declared to be the only Savior by John’s voice, and infinite miracles, and by the testimonies of all the Prophets. But the world notwithstanding being addicted to false prophets, and desirous to seem religious, seeth none of all these things.
43:5:45: This denial doth not put away that which is here said, but correcteth it, as if Christ said, the Jews shall have no sorer an accuser than Moses.
43:6:1: Not that he cut over the lake of Tiberias, but by reason of the large creeks, his sailing made his journey the shorter: therefore he is said to have gone over the sea, when as he passed over from one side of the creek to the other.

And as for that, that Paul 1 Cor. 10 calleth Manna spiritual food, it maketh nothing against this place, for he joineth the thing signified with the sign: but in this whole disputation, Christ dealeth with the Jews after their own opinion and conceit of the matter, and they had no further consideration of the Manna, but in that it fed the belly.
43:6:35: Which have life, and give life.

In the book of the Prophets, for the old Testament was divided by them into three several parts, into the Law the Prophets, and the Holy writ.

Which giveth life to the world.

That is, those things were not yet seen and perceived, which were to show and set forth the glory of the only begotten.

This was some place appointed for the gathering of the offerings.
